title: Bihar Factories Double in 19 Years: A Positive Shift in Industrial Growth
summary: Bihar’s Factories Have Doubled—A Quiet Industrial Comeback Is Taking Shape Bihar is building again.Slowly, steadily, and with renewed confidence. For years, the state stayed away from India’s industrial spotlight. However, fresh data
content:
Bihar’s Factories Have Doubled—A Quiet Industrial Comeback Is Taking Shape

Bihar is building again.Slowly, steadily, and with renewed confidence.

For years, the state stayed away from India’s industrial spotlight. However, fresh data now tells a different story. Bihar is not standing still anymore. Instead, it is laying the foundation for long-term industrial growth.

According to the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) 2023–24, the number of registered factories in Bihar has doubled over the last 19 years. Clearly, this growth reflects a changing economic mindset. More importantly, it signals resilience, recovery, and rising ambition.

A Steady Rise That Signals Structural Change

In 2004–05, Bihar had 1,674 registered factories.Gradually, the number increased.

By 2010–11, it reached 2,805 units.Later, in 2018–19, it touched 3,422 factories.

Then came the pandemic. Like everywhere else, industries faced disruption. Even so, Bihar showed recovery strength. In 2022–23, factories stood at 3,307. Soon after, in 2023–24, the number rose to 3,386, recording a 2.4% annual growth.

Therefore, despite challenges, the growth curve remains upward. That itself speaks volumes.

Bihar’s Position Is Improving on the National Map

Across India, 2,60,061 factories operated in 2023–24. Within this landscape, Bihar’s presence is becoming more visible.

Notably, Bihar has moved ahead of Jharkhand (2,889) and Odisha (3,281) in factory count. This shift highlights consistent improvement. At the same time, it shows how eastern India’s industrial balance is evolving.

While larger states still lead, Bihar’s progress proves that industrial revival does not happen overnight. Instead, it grows layer by layer.

Regional Gains Reflect Growing Industrial Confidence

Surpassing neighbouring states marks a confidence boost.Moreover, it reflects improving policy focus.

States like Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal currently have higher factory numbers. However, Bihar’s advantage lies in its emerging sectors and untapped potential. Therefore, the state stands at a promising inflection point.

With the right push, Bihar can convert momentum into scale.

Emerging Sectors Are Powering the Next Phase

According to Ram Lal Khetan, President of the Bihar Industries Association, eastern India is entering a new industrial phase. Bihar, in particular, holds strong promise.

Currently, sectors such as food processing, packaging, plastics, mineral-based industries, and apparel manufacturing are expanding steadily. Importantly, small and medium enterprises are leading this change.

Meanwhile, improvements in logistics, energy supply, land access, and skill development can accelerate this progress even further.

Factories, Jobs, and a New Economic Narrative

Every new factory adds more than numbers.It creates jobs.It boosts local supply chains.It strengthens confidence.

Therefore, Bihar’s industrial rise is not just about rankings. Instead, it is about opportunity spreading across districts. With sustained reforms and investments, the state’s manufacturing ecosystem can scale faster.

The direction is clear. The foundation is visible. The momentum is real.

Indian Railways has announced a fresh fare hike.As a result, premium train travel from Bihar will now cost more.Moreover, the change takes effect immediately.

Premium Train Fare Hike: What Changed and Why It Matters

Indian Railways has increased fares for premium category trains.Therefore, passengers traveling from Patna to Delhi and Kolkata will feel the impact first.

According to officials, new ticket rates came into force from today.Consequently, Bihar’s busiest routes now reflect higher prices.Most importantly, sleeper and AC passengers will pay more than before.

Born on September 25, 1996, Sarthak Ranjan built his career through discipline and patience.Rather than chasing early attention, he trusted the domestic circuit.

First, he made his T20 debut in the 2015–16 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy.Soon after, he stepped into List A cricket during the 2016–17 Vijay Hazare Trophy.Later, he earned his first-class debut in the 2018–19 Ranji Trophy.

Throughout these stages, Sarthak represented Delhi.This exposure challenged him constantly.As a result, it strengthened both his technique and mindset.

Delhi Premier League: The Breakthrough Phase

While consistency defined his journey, visibility followed later.That moment arrived during the Delhi Premier League (DPL).

In the 2025 season, Sarthak scored around 448 runs in nine matches.More importantly, he delivered under pressure.Match after match, he showed clarity in shot selection.

Because of these performances, franchises took notice.Eventually, KKR acted.

Why the IPL Stage Matters

The Indian Premier League is unforgiving.It tests adaptability, confidence, and resilience.

With Kolkata Knight Riders, Sarthak enters a team known for structured planning.The franchise has consistently backed players who grow through opportunity.

Moreover, the IPL offers exposure that domestic cricket cannot.Every innings gets analysed.Every decision carries weight.

For Sarthak, IPL 2026 is both a challenge and a chance.

What This Means for Bihar Cricket

Bihar has long searched for strong representation at the highest level of Indian cricket.Sarthak Ranjan’s IPL entry signals progress.

It proves that players connected to the state can break through national barriers.It also sends a clear message to young cricketers across Bihar.Consistency still matters.

This moment is not symbolic.It is practical inspiration.

What Comes Next

The IPL will demand immediate impact.Competition will be intense.Expectations will rise quickly.

However, domestic cricket prepares players for pressure.And Sarthak has spent years earning his place.

As IPL 2026 approaches, all eyes will be on how he adapts.Not for headlines—but for performance.

title: Bihar Gov Announces One Crore Jobs in Five Years
summary: Bihar Sets Ambitious Target of One Crore Jobs — A New Promise of Growth and Dignity for Every Household When a state begins talking about jobs in crores, people listen. Yet in
content:
When a state begins talking about jobs in crores, people listen. Yet in Bihar, this announcement feels different. It feels personal. It feels like hope arriving at the doorstep of every young dreamer.

A Clear Roadmap for Jobs and Growth

During the joint address to the State legislature, Governor Arif Mohammad Khan outlined a bold goal — one crore new jobs within five years. He stressed that the administration has already created 50 lakh opportunities, and now aims to double its impact.

Moreover, he backed this vision with updates on welfare schemes, community upliftment, and agricultural gains. These points gave citizens a clearer picture of the direction Bihar wants to move in.

He highlighted ongoing initiatives for women, farmers, and youth. As a result, the roadmap feels more practical than political. It looks like a plan stitched together with real issues at its core.

Women’s Empowerment Driving Social Change

Bihar has taken several steps to uplift women. The Governor emphasised the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojna, under which thousands of women have already received a support amount of ₹10,000. He added that the scheme will soon reach more eligible beneficiaries.

Additionally, he spoke about significant representation for women. There is 50% reservation in local bodies and 35% reservation in government jobs and police services. These measures ensure that women not only participate but also lead.

Uniforms and bicycles for girls continue to boost attendance in schools. These initiatives help bridge long-standing gaps in access and opportunity. Consequently, more girls enter classrooms with confidence.

Electricity, Harmony, and Community Well-Being

The Governor mentioned that every household receives 125 units of free electricity each month. This relief reaches people across all communities — from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes to OBC, EBC, General, and minority groups. Because of this, many families experience reduced monthly burden.

He also spoke about efforts to maintain harmony through fencing of worship areas and graveyards. These steps help communities feel safer and more respected. They also reduce conflicts around shared spaces.

Agriculture Takes Centre Stage With Higher Yields

Agriculture remains the backbone of Bihar. Therefore, the Governor dedicated part of his speech to its rapid transformation. He highlighted that paddy, wheat, and maize production has doubled, while fish production has increased 2.5 times.

Furthermore, the fourth Agricultural Road Map has received a massive approval of ₹1.62 lakh crore. With this investment, farmers will get infrastructure, training, and support for better harvests.

These changes strengthen the vision of a more self-reliant Bihar. They also create indirect jobs across villages, markets, and supply chains.

Leadership Highlights From the Assembly Session

During the session, Nitish Kumar was named Leader of the Assembly, while Tejashwi Yadav assumed the role of Leader of the Opposition. Narendra Narayan Yadav was elected Deputy Speaker. Meanwhile, Prem Kumar took charge as the new Speaker of the Assembly.

Although technical issues disrupted part of the Governor’s address, the Speaker assured strict action. Despite the glitch, the message reached the people — Bihar wants to move forward with fresh energy and urgency.

Be Part of Bihar’s Changing Narrative

Bihar’s story is evolving. It is no longer just about challenges. It’s about resilience, jobs, empowerment, culture, and growth. It’s about a state rewriting its identity with pride.

summary: “A New Chapter for Bihar’s Governance: Mihir Kumar Singh Takes Charge as Development Commissioner” A New Dawn in Bihar’s Administration Big changes often reshape a state’s direction, and this moment feels exactly
content:
“A New Chapter for Bihar’s Governance: Mihir Kumar Singh Takes Charge as Development Commissioner”

A New Dawn in Bihar’s Administration

Big changes often reshape a state’s direction, and this moment feels exactly like that. Bihar begins a fresh chapter as IAS officer Mihir Kumar Singh takes over as the new Development Commissioner of Bihar, replacing S. Siddharth. The appointment marks a major administrative shift, and many citizens now look forward to stronger development momentum across the state.

This decision is part of a larger IAS reshuffle by the new Bihar government. Moreover, the move includes several high-level transfers that aim to streamline departments and accelerate progress.

Who Is Mihir Kumar Singh?

A 1993-batch IAS officer, Mihir Kumar Singh brings decades of hands-on experience to this crucial role. He previously served as the Additional Chief Secretary (Industries Department). He also handled the Transport Department as well as the role of Director General-cum-Chief Vigilance Commissioner in the General Administration Department.

With such extensive exposure, he understands Bihar’s growth challenges and business potential. Therefore, his new role becomes even more important as Bihar pushes for industrial expansion, improved connectivity, and investment-friendly reforms.

Key Transfers Reshaping Bihar’s Bureaucracy

The state government has made several strategic changes:

CK Anil (1991 Batch)

CK Anil, earlier serving as the Advisor at Bihar Rajya Yojna Parishad, now becomes the Additional Chief Secretary of Revenue & Land Reforms Department. This shift signals an increased focus on land management and digital land records.

Dipak Kumar Singh (1992 Batch)

Dipak Kumar Singh, ACS of the Rural Works Department, continues in his core role. However, he also takes charge as DG-cum-Chief Vigilance Commissioner, strengthening internal accountability mechanisms.

Kundan Kumar (2004 Batch)

Kundan Kumar, previously Resident Commissioner (New Delhi), now steps in as the Secretary of Industries Department. He will also continue holding additional charge as Resident Commissioner and MD of BIADA. This combination of roles hints at aggressive industry outreach and investor engagement.

(Tag: #KundanKumarIAS #BIADA)

B Kartikey Dhanji (2008 Batch)

Kartikey Dhanji will now focus entirely on the Minor Irrigation Department, after his additional charge of the Industries Department was relieved.

Sanjay Kumar Singh (2007 Batch)

Sanjay Kumar Singh, Secretary of Commercial Taxes, takes on added responsibility as OSD in the Home Department. This strengthens coordination between taxation, enforcement, and administrative oversight.

Kaushal Kishore (2010 Batch)

Kaushal Kishore, Commissioner of Darbhanga Division, now also handles the charge of Tirhut Commissioner, Muzaffarpur. This decision aims to ensure continuity and smoother regional governance.

Raj Kumar (2010 Batch)

Raj Kumar moves from Tirhut Division to become the new Transport Secretary, a department critical to Bihar’s growing road network and mobility expansion.

Why This Reshuffle Matters for Bihar

This restructuring may appear administrative, but it directly impacts governance quality. New leadership often introduces new energy. Additionally, these officers bring diverse experience from industries, land reforms, transport, rural development, and district administration. Together, they can build faster systems and better services.

People now expect quicker decision-making, stronger vigilance, and more development-driven policies. Since every department connects with the public, these changes could boost efficiency across Bihar’s growth landscape.

content:
A Fresh Wave of Hope: Bihar Moves Toward Digital Growth

Big news often arrives quietly, yet it changes everything. Bihar is now preparing to open three new IT Centers of Excellence, and Jamui stands as one of the proposed locations. This single decision has created fresh curiosity across the region, especially among young learners who want better opportunities in technology.

These centers aim to strengthen digital education, improve skill development, and create a space where students can access industry-ready training. Many districts still lack structured tech facilities, so this move can shift the learning landscape in meaningful ways.

What These IT Centers Could Mean for Students and Job Seekers

Technology-driven careers are expanding rapidly. However, students from smaller towns often struggle to access the necessary training. With the proposed centers, young people may soon learn coding, automation, digital tools, and new-age tech skills closer to home.

Moreover, these hubs can create multiple layers of opportunity. They can support local start-ups, offer digital literacy programs, and inspire young innovators. As a result, families can plan long-term education without needing to migrate immediately.

During her visit to Jamui, the Minister for IT and Sports shared details of this proposal while speaking to residents. The announcement sparked discussions about how such centers could reshape Jamui’s learning ecosystem.

Parallel Push for Sports: Upgrading Local Stadiums and Training Facilities

Alongside IT development, the region may also see new activity in sports infrastructure. Plans include improving existing stadiums and beginning the construction of a new Sports Complex worth ₹3 crore in Jamui. These changes aim to give young athletes better training spaces and access to structured coaching.

For many children, sports remain a powerful path to confidence and discipline. Therefore, upgraded spaces can help nurture talent and create a more active sports culture in the district.

Direct Citizen Access: A Local Office for Public Interaction

During the same visit, the IT and Sports Minister also mentioned that a dedicated office will soon operate in Jamui from 9 AM to 5 PM. Local residents will be able to submit written applications and receive timely responses. This step encourages smoother communication and supports transparent handling of public concerns.

Although the announcement drew attention, the larger focus remained on how the upcoming centers and sports facilities might improve everyday life for students, parents, and young athletes.

Jamui’s Transition: From Aspirations to Actionable Plans

Change takes time. Yet announcements like these show a shift toward structured growth. Jamui’s youth often speak about opportunities they miss due to distance or limited resources. With planned improvements in technology, sports, and public accessibility, the district could move toward a more supportive environment for learning and development.

Residents now wait to see how these plans take shape on the ground. Their expectations remain simple: fair access, reliable facilities, and consistent follow-through.

content:
“46,000 New Healthcare Jobs: Bihar Launches Its Biggest Recruitment Drive Ever — A New Era of Hospitals, Jobs and Hope”

When a state announces over 46,000 new healthcare positions, people listen. But when the announcement comes with clear timelines, fresh infrastructure plans, and rapid progress across departments, it feels like a turning point for every family waiting for better healthcare.

A Massive Recruitment Push That Touches Every Corner of Healthcare

Bihar’s Health Minister Mangal Pandey returned to office with an ambitious goal—strengthen the entire healthcare workforce as fast as possible. He revealed that recruitment exams or advertisements have already been issued for 25 different job categories.

Moreover, these categories range from general duty medical officers to nursing staff, paramedics, dental officers, and even specialist doctors. The scale is huge, and the work has already begun.

Nearly 12,627 technical-level posts have completed examinations. Additionally, recruitment for doctors, nurses, pharmacists and technicians has moved into the final stages, bringing much-needed relief for hospitals across the state.

What’s Filling Up First? A Quick Breakdown

The numbers are impressive, but the speed matters even more.Here’s how the drive is progressing:

title: Bihar Teacher New Transfer Rules 2025: Relief for 22,732 Teacher
summary: “22,732 Bihar Teachers Finally See Movement: New Transfer Rules Bring Real New Year Relief” A Big Shift Begins: 22,732 Bihar Teachers Step Into a New Year of Hope For thousands of teachers
content:
“22,732 Bihar Teachers Finally See Movement: New Transfer Rules Bring Real New Year Relief”

For thousands of teachers across Bihar, the wait felt endless. Transfers got delayed. Families stayed apart. And uncertainty grew every month. Now, at last, a real shift is happening — one that brings clarity, structure, and hope.

Fresh transfer guidelines released this week have changed the mood completely. With clear deadlines and a transparent system, 22,732 teachers can finally prepare for a new beginning.

Clear Timelines Bring Immediate Relief

The Education Department has announced that all transfers will be completed by December 31. The process of school allocation will begin on December 16, and every teacher will join their new posting within the date mentioned in their respective letters.

This decisive timeline reduces anxiety and helps teachers plan their move with ease.

Teachers Can List Five Preferred Blocks

The updated rules allow teachers to choose five preferred blocks within their assigned district. A committee chaired by the District Magistrate will carry out block-wise, class-wise, and subject-wise decisions from December 10 to 15.

Transparent Priority System

To ensure fairness, the Education Department has set a clear order:

Disabled teachers Women with disabilities Other women Men

Men

Additionally, special teachers receive priority above BPSC recruits, while regular teachers remain above both groups. This systematic arrangement ensures smoother and more transparent placements.

A Digital Transfer Workflow for Accuracy

All transfer activities will run through the e-Shiksha Kosh Portal, making the process structured and trackable. District officials will open the Inter District Transfer module, view eligible applicants, check vacancies, and complete block allocation digitally.

This workflow not only reduces manual errors but also builds confidence among teachers waiting for fair allotments.

41,684 Applications Received; Most Already Processed

The scale of the transfer cycle is massive. Between September 5–13, a total of 41,684 teachers applied across elementary, middle, and higher secondary schools. Only Tier-1 and Tier-2 recruits were eligible to participate.

Out of these, 24,732 teachers already have their district allotments finalised.

Teachers left out due to lack of vacancies were later allowed to submit fresh preferences from September 23–30. Because of this extended window, an additional 2,439 teachers will now receive districts, ending a long year of waiting for many families.

This is the third major transfer round since voluntary applications were first enabled through the e-Shiksha Kosh portal in November 2024.

What This Means for Teachers Across Bihar

This shift is more than administrative progress. It brings stability, peace of mind, and a chance for teachers to reconnect with their families. Schools also benefit because teachers who feel settled often teach with more focus and energy.

The improved transfer system signals better coordination across the education network, stronger digital processes, and smoother communication for all stakeholders.

title: WCDC Chief and ADRI Researchers Call for Modern Career Pathways for Bihar’s Women
summary: “Sapne Bade, Mauke Bhi Bade!” — Why Bihar Must Help Women Break Free From Stereotyped Jobs A New Wave of Voices in Patna Patna woke up to a powerful message this week:
content:
A New Wave of Voices in Patna

Patna woke up to a powerful message this week: Bihar’s women deserve careers beyond the narrow lanes of “stereotyped” work. At an ADRI panel discussion in the city on November 20, 2025, WCDC Managing Director Bandana Preyashi strongly urged the state to act faster and smarter. Her words created a moment that hit both the mind and the heart.

She said women still get pushed toward the same old roles. Beauty work. Tailoring. Basic support jobs. However, their dreams now stretch far wider. Many want modern roles like computer operators, digital service providers, and office administrators. They want dignity, skill, and a future.

The Core Issue: Skills Are Missing, Not Aspirations

Preyashi explained the real problem. Women want to grow. The government wants them to dream big. Yet the skill gap blocks their journey. As a result, they cannot reach the jobs they truly want.She framed it bluntly: “We haven’t been able to help women realise the very aspirations we ask them to seek.”

This gap restricts thousands of marginalised women who want dignified and better-paid work. And this is exactly where Bihar must step up with urgency.

New Research Reveals a Hidden Pattern

The event began with a joint research presentation by ADRI and the University of Reading (@UniofReading).Dr. Ashmita Gupta (@ADRI_Official) highlighted an important pattern. She said aspirations in Bihar still depend heavily on gender, caste and exposure. Wages matter, but not as much as many assume. Because of limited awareness, people mainly hope for jobs they hear about often — especially uniformed roles or government posts.

This insight surprised many attendees, yet it also opened the door for deeper conversations.

Why Limited Exposure Shapes Dreams

Professor Kambhampati (@UniofReading) added a strong perspective. She explained that people can aspire only to what they understand. When women lack exposure, they cannot imagine possibilities beyond their neighbourhoods.

She described it simply:“To aspire, you must first know what the ideal looks like and how to reach it.”

Therefore, expanding awareness becomes as important as giving training. Without both, Bihar will continue to see restricted ambitions, especially among women.

A Room Full of Changemakers

The panel also included Prem Prakash (NITI Aayog Bihar), Dr. Sunita Lall, and Dr. Ushasi Gupta. Academics, students, civil society members and policymakers filled the room. Because of their shared concern, the discussion grew energetic and solution-focused.

Everyone agreed that if Bihar wants a stronger labour market, it must close the ambition gap. It must also improve access to non-traditional work pathways. Most importantly, it must give women the skills and exposure that unlock modern careers.

The Bigger Picture for Bihar’s Future

This conversation signals something bigger. Bihar is rewriting its story every day. Women stand at the centre of that transformation. However, they still need a bridge — a bridge connecting dreams with opportunities.

When Bihar expands training, breaks stereotypes and celebrates modern careers, women rise. And when women rise, families rise. Entire communities rise. Ultimately, the state rises.

summary: Revolutionising Bihar’s Land Survey: Free 3-Month Installation & Diploma Course Backed by Survey of India and Indian Institute of Technology Patna Imagine walking through Bihar’s fields, riversides and mines — and watching
content:
Revolutionising Bihar’s Land Survey: Free 3-Month Installation & Diploma Course Backed by Survey of India and Indian Institute of Technology Patna

Imagine walking through Bihar’s fields, riversides and mines — and watching precision technology reveal what the eye can’t. Right now, thanks to a new initiative, survey personnel in Bihar will gain that power. Indeed, the collaboration between the Survey of India and IIT Patna is set to transform how we map, monitor and manage land in the state.

Why This Matters for Bihar

Bihar has long faced challenges in land-management: changing river courses, flood threat, unauthorised mining, and outdated maps. So when the Survey of India offered a three-month free installation of a continuous reference station system, and IIT Patna hosted a workshop on geospatial data and land surveying in Patna, we hit a milestone.The workshop, held in the state capital, brought together experts to discuss how survey technology can deliver fast, precise data — with accuracy up to three centimetres. This is a major leap over older methods.

What the Programme Offers

The Survey of India will provide free installation of the reference station system (for three months) as part of the campaign. The diploma course (40–80 hours) will be run jointly by IIT Patna and Survey of India at low cost for land-surveying personnel. The technology aims to expedite data collection without needing external reference. As Director Prof. T.N. Singh of IIT Patna explained: this system can monitor river water levels, mining activity, bridges and transport infrastructure. With accuracy down to three centimetres, mapping and processing systems will see a quantum leap — aligning Bihar’s infrastructure and land-use monitoring with global standards.

Fields of Application – A Game Changer

Agriculture

When farmers and officials have extremely precise land and water-data, they can make smarter decisions — such as optimising irrigation based on exact field contours, or mapping soil changes.

Flood Management & Rivers

If a reference station sits on a riverbank, it can tell today’s water volume and estimate tomorrow’s. With floods frequent in Bihar, this tool gives early warning and stronger planning.

Mining & Sand Extraction

As the system monitors mining zones like sand-extraction areas, it can flag daily extraction volumes and prevent illicit operations. This makes the task safer, faster, and less labour-intensive.

Infrastructure & Environment

Bridges, roads, transport hubs, environmental studies — all benefit from precise geospatial data. For Bihar’s push to modernise, this is foundational.

How Survey Professionals Can Benefit

If you work in land-surveying, revenue, mapping or fieldwork in Bihar, this course and installation offer is a real opportunity. With the diploma from IIT Patna + Survey of India, you acquire recognised credentials. With reference-station technology you gain hands-on with next-gen equipment. And with three-month free install you can pilot and prove this in your region before full rollout.

What You Should Do Next

title: Siwan’s Railway Heroes Win Safety Star Award
summary: “Bihar Heroes on Track: Siwan’s Railway Workers Win Safety Star Award for Their Quick Action and Courage” A Spark That Could Have Been a Disaster – Saved by Bihar’s Brave Railway Workers
content:
“Bihar Heroes on Track: Siwan’s Railway Workers Win Safety Star Award for Their Quick Action and Courage”

A Spark That Could Have Been a Disaster – Saved by Bihar’s Brave Railway Workers

In a state often defined by its resilience, Bihar’s Siwan district once again proved that dedication and alertness can prevent disaster. On July 9, when fire broke out near the railway tracks close to Panchrukhi station, Gatekeeper Dilawar Hussain noticed the flames and acted immediately. Without hesitation, he informed the railway control room and ensured that the track was secured before any train passed. His swift decision saved lives, property, and ensured the safety of hundreds of passengers.

This act of presence of mind didn’t go unnoticed. The North Eastern Railway (NER) recognized him, along with two other Siwan-based railway workers, for their exceptional vigilance and awarded them the “Safety Star of the Month.”

Honouring Bihar’s Safety Stars

On November 11, at the North Eastern Railway Headquarters in Gorakhpur, General Manager Uday Borwankar felicitated the awardees in a special ceremony. He emphasized that safety remains the top priority of Indian Railways, and employees who perform their duties with sincerity and promptness serve as true inspirations for others.

Among those honoured were:

Dilawar Hussain (Gateman, 83-C Siwan): Detected and reported the fire near Panchrukhi station on time. Om Prakash Kumar (Gateman, 4-C): Found a crack in the rail weld between Amalori Sarsar and Hathua on June 29 and repaired it immediately using a jogul plate. Nehal Ahmad: Alerted authorities about a rail fracture at Siwan Junction on August 25, preventing a major accident.

title: Discover how NIOS and IHCNBT are reviving Nalanda’s legacy in modern education
summary: Echoes of Nalanda: Where Ancient Wisdom Meets Modern Minds Centuries before global universities existed, Nalanda stood tall as a beacon of knowledge and intellectual freedom. Today, its legacy is making a comeback
content:
Echoes of Nalanda: Where Ancient Wisdom Meets Modern Minds

Centuries before global universities existed, Nalanda stood tall as a beacon of knowledge and intellectual freedom. Today, its legacy is making a comeback — not as ruins of the past, but as a living philosophy reshaping modern education in India.

The roots of monastic learning stretch back to Buddhist viharas from the 5th century BCE. These early centers of meditation soon became structured institutions teaching ethics, philosophy, and logic. Over time, renowned universities like Nalanda, Vikramashila, and Takshashila became magnets for scholars across Asia. Their approach was holistic — valuing moral discipline, intellectual debate, and lifelong learning — qualities still vital for modern classrooms.

Nalanda: The World’s First Multidisciplinary University

While earlier monasteries focused mainly on spiritual growth, Nalanda Mahavihara (5th–12th century CE) broke new ground. It offered a residential, organized, and secular curriculum that taught grammar, medicine, astronomy, mathematics, and the arts alongside Buddhist philosophy.

What made Nalanda revolutionary was its inclusive and dialogic learning model. Debates, discussions, and commentaries were central to its pedagogy. Students came from China, Korea, Tibet, and Southeast Asia — a true example of global education before globalization. Education here wasn’t about sectarianism; it was a pursuit of universal enlightenment blending faith and reason.

Modern Revival: NIOS and IHCNBT Bring Monastic Learning into the National Framework

In the spirit of Nalanda, the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS), in collaboration with the Indian Himalayan Council of Nalanda Buddhist Tradition (IHCNBT), has launched a landmark initiative. Their mission? To modernize and formally recognize monastic education across India.

Traditionally conducted in Bhoti, this system preserves Buddhist teachings and classical Indian literature — from Nagarjuna and Dharmakirti to timeless Sanskrit works like Ramayana and Meghaduta. Now, this intellectual treasure is being aligned with modern academic frameworks at the Elementary, Secondary, and Senior Secondary levels.

Rajeev Kumar Singh, Director (Academics) at NIOS, calls it “a bridge between ancient wisdom and modern opportunity.” He emphasizes that the initiative is not about secularizing Buddhism but about empowering learners and giving equal recognition to traditional knowledge in today’s education system.

Preserving Culture, Strengthening Identity

The IHCNBT, representing Buddhist communities across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and North Bengal, plays a pivotal role in this educational renaissance. For Maling Gombu, General Secretary of IHCNBT, the initiative is both patriotic and cultural. It strengthens India’s identity as the birthplace of great learning traditions and ensures that monasteries remain active centers of knowledge.

Today, 132 monasteries across the Himalayas have been accredited by NIOS, enrolling nearly 10,000 learners. This movement is not just an administrative reform — it’s a cultural revival. The Bodh Darshan initiative dignifies centuries-old Himalayan education systems, reaffirming India’s position as the spiritual and intellectual cradle of Buddhist thought.

Nalanda’s Spirit Lives On

As the world searches for balance between technology and wisdom, Nalanda’s philosophy offers a timeless solution — education that nourishes both intellect and soul. Its revival through NIOS and IHCNBT is more than policy; it’s a return to India’s roots in value-based, inclusive learning.

title: Bihar Sees Highest-Ever Voter Turnout Of 64.66% In Phase 1
summary: Bihar Votes with Heart: Record 64.66% Turnout Reflects a New Wave of Awareness Bihar made history today.With 64.66% voter turnout in the first phase of the 2025 Assembly Elections, the state witnessed
content:
Bihar Votes with Heart: Record 64.66% Turnout Reflects a New Wave of Awareness

Bihar made history today.With 64.66% voter turnout in the first phase of the 2025 Assembly Elections, the state witnessed its highest-ever participation in a state election. For a land often stereotyped for its politics, this number tells a deeper story — one of awareness, change, and rising political consciousness.

From Apathy to Action: Bihar’s Voters Step Forward

According to the Election Commission, the 64.66% turnout surpassed all previous state records, beating the 62.57% turnout in 2000 and even the 64.6% seen in the 1998 Lok Sabha polls.Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar expressed gratitude to voters and poll staff, acknowledging their role in this democratic celebration.

This surge comes after a special revision of the voter list, which removed 47 lakh names. Many critics argued the move would suppress turnout, especially among poor and marginalized communities. Yet, Bihar turned up stronger. The passion for change clearly outshined the numbers on paper.

A Closer Look at Bihar’s Political Pulse

Historically, higher voter turnouts in Bihar have signaled waves of transformation. In 2010, Nitish Kumar’s JD(U), allied with the BJP, won big with just 52.73% turnout.In 2015, when Nitish switched sides to ally with Lalu Yadav’s RJD, turnout jumped by over 4%, and the alliance triumphed.Five years later, he realigned with the BJP, and despite a slight increase in turnout, his party lost 28 seats — showing that numbers alone don’t decide the outcome.

Now, in 2025, the first-phase turnout is 7.37% higher than the 2020 overall average. That’s not a small leap — it’s a sign of re-engagement, especially among first-time and rural voters.

Anti-Incumbency or Reclaimed Trust?

Conventional wisdom says a high turnout often means anti-incumbency. However, Bihar’s story might not be that simple.Across India, states like Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh saw higher turnouts but voted for the same party again. Bihar could follow a similar pattern — or rewrite its own.

For the Mahagathbandhan, led by Tejashwi Yadav, this turnout might be an encouraging sign. He’s contesting from his family bastion, Raghopur, which has consistently favored the Yadav legacy. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary (BJP) and folk icon Maithili Thakur, contesting from Alinagar, also drew heavy local attention.

Each ballot cast today carries emotion — frustration, hope, and belief — all stitched together into one powerful democratic act.

The Road Ahead: Bihar’s Story Isn’t Over Yet

Only 121 out of 243 constituencies have voted so far. The remaining half will go to polls on November 11, and results will be declared on November 14.What happens next could redefine the political balance of Bihar.

But beyond parties and alliances, this turnout stands as a tribute to every voter who chose action over apathy.Bihar is not just voting — it’s speaking. Loudly, clearly, and with purpose.

title: Patna Municipal Corporation Launches Massive Anti-Dengue Drive
summary: Patna’s War on Dengue: Patna Municipal Corporation’s 18,000-Home Daily Blitz to Defeat Mosquito Menace A City at War — And Everyone’s Involved Every dawn in Patna now begins with action. Streets echo
content:
A City at War — And Everyone’s Involved

Every dawn in Patna now begins with action. Streets echo with the hum of fogging machines, and residents watch as civic workers spray every corner. The Patna Municipal Corporation (PMC), under the leadership of Municipal Commissioner Yashpal Meena, has launched a war-level anti-dengue drive, reaching 18,000 homes daily.

Unlike previous seasonal clean-ups, this mission is intense, structured, and city-wide. Teams are not only eliminating larvae but also spreading awareness door-to-door. The aim is clear — stop dengue before it starts.

Coordinated Effort: 375 Teams, Two Shifts, One Goal

To ensure complete coverage, five anti-larva teams have been deployed in every ward. In high-risk dengue areas, ten special units now work round the clock. The teams check rooftops, pots, overhead tanks, and under-construction sites — all potential breeding spots.

Across 75 municipal wards, 375 teams operate in two shifts daily. They use Temephos for larva control and Malathion for fogging. Meanwhile, a special 500-metre perimeter is sprayed around every dengue-positive home identified by the health department.

This coordinated rhythm of inspection, fogging, and verification ensures that no neighbourhood is left behind.

Hospitals on High Alert

Hospitals, often overlooked breeding grounds, are receiving special focus. Dedicated workers visit PMCH, NMCH, AIIMS, IGIMS, IGIC, Gardiner Hospital, and Rajvanshi Nagar Hospital daily for spraying and fogging.

This hospital-level vigilance reduces infection risk for patients and frontline workers. Moreover, it prevents re-infestation from within high-traffic healthcare zones — a crucial step that strengthens Patna’s overall defence.

Vehicles, Zones, and Rapid Response

The civic body has also mobilised 57 fogging vehicles across six major zones:

Pataliputra Zone – 13 vehicles Nutan Rajdhani Zone – 12 vehicles Azimabad Zone – 7 vehicles Patna City Zone – 6 vehicles Kankarbagh Zone – 10 vehicles Bankipur Zone – 9 vehicles

Pataliputra Zone – 13 vehicles

Nutan Rajdhani Zone – 12 vehicles

Azimabad Zone – 7 vehicles

Patna City Zone – 6 vehicles

Kankarbagh Zone – 10 vehicles

Bankipur Zone – 9 vehicles

Every evening, these vehicles move through colonies, markets, and schools, ensuring consistent coverage. Furthermore, each team maintains a logbook for citizen feedback. Random verification calls confirm that ground operations match official reports.

If residents face issues, they can call toll-free number 155304, and a rapid-response unit reaches the location the same day. This real-time grievance redressal has made citizens active partners in the drive.

From Awareness to Action

While PMC’s machinery is vast, the true strength lies in citizen cooperation. Commissioner Yashpal Meena repeatedly urges residents to keep their surroundings clean and water-free. Stagnant water, even in a bottle cap, can become a breeding ground within days.

Therefore, small daily habits — covering tanks, cleaning trays, and removing puddles — directly reduce dengue risk. Additionally, responding to fogging teams and sharing feedback builds trust and helps improve the process.

Together, these collective actions transform awareness into sustained prevention.

The Bigger Picture: Patna’s Health Revival

Beyond dengue, this campaign reflects a changing mindset in Patna’s civic governance. It shows urgency, data-driven planning, and citizen-centric response — values that define a modern city.

From fogging lanes to verifying calls, every small act adds up to a safer, cleaner, and healthier Patna. The anti-dengue drive is not just a seasonal measure anymore; it’s a public movement that places health at the core of city life.

Be Part of the Movement

The fight against dengue needs every hand, every household, and every neighbourhood.Cooperate. Stay aware. Stay proactive. Together, we can make Patna mosquito-free.

content:
A City on the Move

Drive through Patna today, and you can feel the pulse of change. The capital of Bihar isn’t standing still anymore—it’s evolving fast. The city is preparing for a major transformation under Chief Minister Nitish Kumar’s Pragati Yatra on February 21, where projects worth nearly ₹1,350 crore will be launched.

Among these initiatives are a multi-modal hub, a model vending zone, and an elevated road near the airport—each one crafted to ease congestion and modernize city life. Together, they mark a turning point for Patna’s urban future.

Multi-Modal Hub: Where All Roads Meet

Patna’s upcoming multi-modal hub will unify the way people move. It’s designed to bring buses, autos, e-rickshaws, and inter-city transport under one modern roof.

The plan includes a multi-level complex near GPO, linked to Patna Junction through a pedestrian subway. It will feature digital displays, elevators, EV charging bays, and spacious waiting zones. Moreover, real-time coordination between transit modes will cut travel time significantly.

This is not just a structure—it’s a statement of intent. As traffic density grows, the hub will simplify commutes, reduce chaos, and create a smoother, greener mobility experience for citizens.

Model Vending Zone: Empowering the Heart of the Market

Patna’s streets have long been a mix of energy and congestion. Street vendors bring life to the city, yet the lack of structured space has caused frequent traffic snarls.

To address this, the administration is developing model vending zones that balance order with opportunity. Vendors will now operate from well-defined stalls with lighting, sanitation, and storage facilities. Additionally, proper footpaths will return to pedestrians, easing both movement and safety.

This initiative celebrates inclusivity. Instead of displacing traders, it integrates them into a cleaner, more organized ecosystem—preserving livelihoods while reshaping urban flow.

Elevated Road Near Airport: A Gateway to Global Patna

The new elevated road near Jay Prakash Narayan Airport is another bold step forward. With passenger traffic rising after the new terminal opening, this link will ensure swift and seamless access.

The project envisions a four-lane elevated corridor that cuts travel time from city centers to the airport dramatically. Furthermore, it connects to broader infrastructure goals under the Patna Ring Road plan, strengthening routes to Bihta and beyond.

For travelers, this means fewer jams and quicker routes. For businesses, it’s a sign that Patna is ready for global attention.

A Ripple Effect Across Rural Patna

While urban projects take the spotlight, rural Patna isn’t left behind. A new road will soon link the Bihta–Sarmera route with Daniyawan Top, improving inter-block travel. Local residents near Naubatpur have also been advocating for a flyover at Nispura Lakh—a long-pending demand that might finally see approval.

Additionally, large ponds and lakes are being rejuvenated under MNREGA and Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali Yojana, supporting both irrigation and ecology. These parallel efforts ensure that growth spreads evenly, not just within the city but across the district.

Why It Matters: Patna’s Image Is Changing

This transformation is more than construction—it’s confidence in motion. For years, Patna has battled the stereotype of being “slow to grow.” Now, these projects show a city stepping into its own, ready to attract investors, students, and entrepreneurs.

Every bridge, road, and zone adds a layer of pride. And as these developments unfold, they redefine Bihar’s identity on the national map—not as a story of catching up, but of leading ahead.

content:

Patna’s Women Power Takes Global Stage

These serve women during festivals, fairs, and public events — offering them clean, secure spaces when they need them most. Currently, eight Pink Toilets (four mobile, two permanent, and two Loo Cafés) are operational across Patna. title: Bihar EOU blocks over 20,000 mobile numbers in cybercrime crackdown
summary: A Digital Tsunami Hits Bihar The digital storm landed hard in Bihar—and this time, it wasn’t business as usual. The Economic Offences Unit (EOU) has deactivated over 20,000 mobile numbers, blocked more
content:
A Digital Tsunami Hits Bihar

The digital storm landed hard in Bihar—and this time, it wasn’t business as usual. The Economic Offences Unit (EOU) has deactivated over 20,000 mobile numbers, blocked more than 13,000 IMEIs, and frozen crores in bank accounts to clamp down on cybercrime. This decisive action shows Bihar is no longer a passive victim—it’s fighting back with precision and purpose.

Inside the Crackdown: The Numbers Tell a Story

From January to September 2025, Bihar logged around 74,000 online fraud complaints. The EOU responded decisively, freezing ₹75.92 crore—just over 21% of reported losses—and returning ₹5.14 crore to victims.

In October alone, 249 mobile numbers linked to online scams were deactivated. The department has also begun a rigorous investigation into “mule accounts,” which are bank accounts used to launder fraudulent money. In August, officials flagged nearly 200 such accounts and retrieved information on 138 of them through national data systems.

Furthermore, over 513 social media posts and profiles spreading misinformation or promoting scams have been removed. Every measure adds another layer of protection for Bihar’s digital citizens.

Why This Crackdown Matters

1. Rising Threats in the Digital Era

Bihar’s growing internet reach has brought new challenges. While access improves lives, it also exposes users to phishing, fake investment schemes, and online job scams. Many victims come from semi-urban and rural backgrounds, where digital literacy remains low.

2. A Statewide Impact

Cybercrime isn’t confined to Patna or urban centers. Small towns and villages have also faced the brunt of fraudsters targeting unsuspecting users. This crackdown sends a clear message—no corner of Bihar is off the radar.

3. Building Digital Trust

The EOU’s ongoing actions reinforce public faith in the system. By tracking transactions, blocking devices, and freezing suspicious accounts, authorities are restoring confidence in online financial activity and digital safety.

Step-by-Step: How the EOU Is Winning the Battle

Mobile number blocking: Over 20,000 SIM cards linked to scams deactivated. IMEI lockdown: More than 13,000 mobile devices rendered unusable. Mule account investigation: Hundreds of suspicious bank accounts flagged and data retrieved. Fund recovery: ₹75.92 crore frozen, ₹5.14 crore already returned to victims. Social media monitoring: Over 500 misleading profiles and posts removed.

Mobile number blocking: Over 20,000 SIM cards linked to scams deactivated.

IMEI lockdown: More than 13,000 mobile devices rendered unusable.

Mule account investigation: Hundreds of suspicious bank accounts flagged and data retrieved.

Fund recovery: ₹75.92 crore frozen, ₹5.14 crore already returned to victims.

Social media monitoring: Over 500 misleading profiles and posts removed.

Each of these steps pushes Bihar closer to a secure and accountable digital space.

What It Means for Citizens

Every digital user in Bihar plays a role in this transformation. Awareness and caution are now vital weapons. Avoid sharing OTPs, clicking unknown links, or trusting random investment calls. If a message or transaction feels suspicious, report it immediately.

This campaign proves something powerful—when technology is misused, Bihar will act. With the EOU leading from the front, the message is unmistakable: cybercriminals can no longer hide behind screens.

title: IIT Patna & Amity University sign MoU to Revolutionize Teacher Education in Bihar
summary: IIT Patna and Amity University Collaborate to Transform Teacher Education Patna is witnessing a remarkable step in teacher education. IIT Patna and Amity University Patna have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding
content:
IIT Patna and Amity University Collaborate to Transform Teacher Education

Patna is witnessing a remarkable step in teacher education. IIT Patna and Amity University Patna have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate under the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP) sponsored by the University Grants Commission (UGC). This partnership promises to empower teachers with advanced skills, research opportunities, and innovative training aligned with National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

The MoU was signed by Prof. T. N. Singh, Director of IIT Patna, and Prof. (Dr.) Vivekanand Pandey, Vice Chancellor of Amity University Patna. The event gathered senior faculty members, officials, and the Program Director of MMTTC at IIT Patna, reflecting a strong commitment to improving teacher quality and higher education in Bihar.

Focus on Research, Innovation, and Practical Learning

According to Prof. T. N. Singh, this collaboration will integrate research and innovation into teacher training programs. He emphasized that the initiative will not only benefit educators in Bihar but also create ripple effects across India. Furthermore, the MoU encourages practical learning and introduces contemporary teaching methods, helping educators make meaningful contributions to society.

Transitioning from traditional training, teachers will now gain access to cutting-edge workshops, seminars, and research projects. These initiatives will enhance the quality of education delivered in classrooms and prepare teachers to handle diverse learning environments efficiently.

Empowering Faculty and Elevating Excellence

Prof. (Dr.) Vivekanand Pandey highlighted that the partnership will focus on faculty empowerment. Joint curriculum improvements and collaborative research projects will foster continuous learning for educators. In addition, these efforts aim to create an ecosystem of innovation, where teachers can implement creative strategies and actively participate in educational reforms.

The MoU ensures structured opportunities for teachers to enhance their professional development. Moreover, it strengthens Bihar’s position as a hub for high-quality education and teacher training. Students, in turn, benefit directly from better-trained educators equipped to meet modern learning demands.

Workshops, Seminars, and Continuous Learning

One of the key pillars of this collaboration includes organizing joint workshops and seminars. These platforms will allow educators to share insights, explore new teaching methodologies, and engage in meaningful dialogue. Additionally, the partnership encourages research collaborations to address real-world challenges in education.

By focusing on continuous learning and innovation, IIT Patna and Amity University are setting a new benchmark for teacher training programs. This initiative aligns perfectly with the broader goals of NEP 2020 and ensures a modern, effective, and practical approach to teaching.

IIT Patna and Amity University Patna are leading the charge to reshape teacher education in Bihar. With this MoU, educators can access innovative resources, research-driven programs, and collaborative learning opportunities.

summary: Patna Sahib to Glow with 11,000 Diyas This Diwali – A Unique Eco-Friendly Celebration at Takht Shri Harmandir Patna Sahib to Shine with 11,000 Diyas This Diwali – Celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas
content:
Patna Sahib to Shine with 11,000 Diyas This Diwali – Celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas in an Eco-Friendly Way

A Bandi Chhor Divas Like Never Before

This year, Patna Sahib will witness a spectacular celebration as Takht Shri Harmandir is lit with 11,000 diyas for Bandi Chhor Divas. The festival isn’t just about lights; it’s a conscious effort to promote eco-friendly celebrations and environmental awareness. Devotees from across India are preparing with excitement to be part of this unique event.

Eco-Friendly Diwali Initiative

The gurudwara management committee has introduced an innovative approach to this year’s celebrations. All 11,000 diyas are traditional clay lamps, reducing environmental impact. The initiative encourages communities to celebrate Diwali sustainably, spreading a powerful message of green living alongside devotion.

Religious Significance

Bandi Chhor Divas marks the historic release of Guru Hargobind Sahib, the sixth Sikh Guru, from Gwalior Fort by Emperor Jahangir. Guru Sahib also freed 52 other kings, demonstrating compassion and justice. Since then, Sikhs commemorate this day by lighting diyas, praying, and holding community gatherings, blending history and spiritual devotion.

Special Programs at Takht Shri Harmandir

On Bandi Chhor Divas, Takht Shri Harmandir will host bhajan-kirtan, spiritual discourses, and a special langar for devotees. Sikh families from all over India participate, creating a vibrant and united celebration that highlights the festival’s religious and cultural significance.

Tradition of Diyas at Home

Families bring a lit diya from their home to the gurudwara, then light all other diyas at home with it. This sacred flame is believed to bring happiness, prosperity, and peace. Homes are also decorated with rangoli, adding color and joy to the festival.

Join the Celebration

Be part of this eco-friendly Bandi Chhor Divas and witness Takht Shri Harmandir illuminated by 11,000 diyas. Carry the flame of devotion and awareness back to your home, and celebrate tradition sustainably.

title: ECI Declares Paid Holiday for All Employees in Bihar on Polling Days
summary: ECI Declares Paid Holiday for All Bihar Employees on Polling Days — Empowering Every Voter The Election Commission of India (ECI) has taken a strong step to boost voter turnout in Bihar.
content:
ECI Declares Paid Holiday for All Bihar Employees on Polling Days — Empowering Every Voter

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has taken a strong step to boost voter turnout in Bihar. It has announced that all employees in the state, including daily and casual workers, will get a paid holiday on polling days during the upcoming General Assembly elections and bye-elections across eight constituencies.

This proactive move aims to remove one of the biggest hurdles in voting — work commitments — and ensure that every eligible citizen gets the time and freedom to vote.

Mark the Polling Dates and Plan Ahead

The ECI wants citizens to prepare early for the elections.

Phase I: November 6, 2025 (Thursday) Phase II and Bye-Elections: November 11, 2025 (Tuesday)

Phase I: November 6, 2025 (Thursday)

Phase II and Bye-Elections: November 11, 2025 (Tuesday)

By giving this clarity well in advance, the Commission hopes voters will plan their day and make voting a priority rather than an afterthought.

Legal Protection Under Section 135B

The decision comes under Section 135B of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which legally requires employers to grant a paid holiday to every employee who is entitled to vote.

If an employer denies this right or deducts wages for the day, strict action can follow. The ECI’s clear message is simple — voting is not just a right, it’s a protected duty.

Who Benefits from This Initiative

This paid holiday extends far beyond government offices.It includes:

Public and Private Sector Employees Daily Wage and Casual Workers Employees Working Outside Their Constituency but Registered in Bihar

Public and Private Sector Employees

Daily Wage and Casual Workers

Employees Working Outside Their Constituency but Registered in Bihar

Even those working in industrial or commercial establishments outside their voting area can now take leave without losing pay. This ensures that no voter is left behind.

Strengthening Democracy, One Vote at a Time

By ensuring that financial worries do not stop people from voting, the ECI is strengthening democracy at the grassroots. Many voters, especially those from the informal sector, often skip voting due to the fear of wage loss.

Now, with paid leave guaranteed, every individual can contribute to shaping Bihar’s political future.

Moreover, this decision reflects how institutions like the Election Commission of India are actively promoting inclusive participation in elections — not just by urging people to vote, but by removing barriers that stop them.

title: Top 5 Crops That Make Bihar an ‘Agri Powerhouse’ Beyond Makhana and Litchi
summary: Bihar’s Fields Tell a Bigger Story When you think of Bihar, two names usually come up — Makhana and Litchi.However, the state’s story doesn’t stop there. Over the years, Bihar has emerged
content:
Bihar’s Fields Tell a Bigger Story

When you think of Bihar, two names usually come up — Makhana and Litchi.However, the state’s story doesn’t stop there. Over the years, Bihar has emerged as one of India’s most dynamic agricultural powerhouses. Its farmers are now combining traditional knowledge with modern farming techniques, transforming the state into a leader across multiple crops.

Let’s take a closer look at the five crops that make Bihar the pride of Indian agriculture.

1. Litchi — The Royal Fruit with Global Appeal

The world knows Bihar for its Shahi Litchi, a fruit so special that it carries a Geographical Indication (GI) tag. Every year, the state produces 3 to 3.22 lakh tonnes, contributing nearly 43% of India’s total litchi output.

Moreover, Bihar’s litchi isn’t confined to Indian markets. It travels to the UK, UAE, Nepal, France, and Australia, earning foreign exchange and fame for local farmers. Thanks to its flavor and freshness, the “Shahi Litchi” has become Bihar’s sweet ambassador across continents.

2. Makhana — The White Gold of Mithila

Next comes Mithila Makhana, another gem that carries a GI tag and deep cultural roots. Bihar contributes 80–90% of India’s total makhana production. The state annually produces around 10,000–1,20,000 tonnes of seeds and nearly 40,000 tonnes of processed makhana.

Beyond domestic markets, Mithila’s Makhana is exported to the USA, UAE, Canada, and Australia. Farmers call it “white gold” — a symbol of pride and prosperity. Over time, it has also turned into one of India’s fastest-growing superfoods, loved for its nutrition and crunch.

3. Mushroom — The New Face of Bihar’s Farming

In recent years, Bihar has turned its attention to mushroom cultivation — and the results are impressive. Since 2021, mushroom production has grown rapidly, positioning Bihar among India’s top producers.

Every year, the state produces around 28,000–41,000 tonnes, accounting for 10–12% of India’s total yield. Farmers primarily grow Button and Oyster mushrooms, using low-cost sheds and modern composting methods. As a result, mushrooms from Bihar now reach West Bengal, Jharkhand, and even countries like Japan and Nepal.

Clearly, Bihar is no longer relying only on traditional crops — it’s experimenting, innovating, and thriving.

4. Singhada (Water Chestnut) — Turning Water into Wealth

Bihar’s wetlands have found a new treasure — Singhada (Water Chestnut). The state produces 50,000–1,00,000 tonnes annually, and about 80% of this comes from North Bihar.

Because of its high demand and easy adaptability, Singhada has become a profitable choice for small-scale farmers. The fruit now travels to the US, UK, Canada, Saudi Arabia, and Singapore. With proper packaging and cold-chain facilities, this aquatic crop has turned stagnant ponds into sources of steady income.

5. Bottle Gourd — A Common Crop with Uncommon Impact

The humble Bottle Gourd (Lauki) might not sound glamorous, yet it has immense value. Bihar produces 6.5 to 6.6 lakh tonnes annually, contributing nearly 20% of India’s total yield.

Because of the state’s fertile Gangetic plains, Lauki thrives throughout the summer and monsoon seasons. Most of the production serves local markets, but Bihar also exports to Bangladesh and Nepal. In a health-conscious world, where demand for light, nutritious food is growing, Lauki gives Bihar another strong edge.

Bihar’s Power Beyond the Top Five

The list doesn’t end here. Bihar ranks second in Jute and Mesta production and third in Potato, Lentil, Green Chili, Okra, and Cauliflower. It also ranks fourth in fruits and vegetables such as Mango, Onion, Carrot, and Eggplant, and fifth in Sunflower, Sugarcane, and Maize.

Such variety proves that Bihar is not just sustaining agriculture — it is leading it through diversity.

What Makes Bihar’s Agriculture So Strong?

Several factors have fueled Bihar’s agricultural transformation:

Fertile alluvial soil and rich water resources from the Ganga plains. Government initiatives supporting irrigation, subsidies, and crop diversification. Farmers adopting modern techniques like drip irrigation and organic farming. Expanding export opportunities that link Bihar’s produce to global markets.

Fertile alluvial soil and rich water resources from the Ganga plains.

Government initiatives supporting irrigation, subsidies, and crop diversification.

Farmers adopting modern techniques like drip irrigation and organic farming.

Expanding export opportunities that link Bihar’s produce to global markets.

Furthermore, the shift from traditional methods to smart, scientific farming has boosted both productivity and profitability. Bihar’s farmlands are no longer seen as outdated — they are symbols of innovation and sustainability.

❤️ The Soul of Bihar’s Soil

Once labeled as a backward state, Bihar is now scripting a remarkable turnaround through agriculture. From Shahi Litchi to Mithila Makhana, and from Mushrooms to Singhada, every crop carries the essence of Bihar’s determination and progress.

AIIMS Patna Turns Pink: Doctors Lead Inspiring Walk to Raise Breast Cancer Awareness

Organized by the Department of Radiation Oncology, the event celebrated Breast Cancer Awareness Month, reminding everyone that early detection can save lives.

A Walk for Hope and Health

The “Pink Walk” began from the institute’s Admin Block and concluded at the OPD Foyer, where pink balloons were released—symbols of solidarity and strength.Leading the initiative were Executive Director (Brig.) Dr. Raju Agarwal, Medical Superintendent Dr. Anup Kumar, Dean of Academics Dr. Poonam Bhadani, and Head of Radiation Oncology Dr. Pritanjali Singh.

Alongside them, several senior doctors — including Dr. Nilesh Mani, Dr. Harikesh Bahadur Singh, Dr. Minakshi Mishra, Dr. Upasna (Radiology), Dr. Veena (Plastic Surgery), and Dr. Azhar (Surgical Oncology) — shared their insights on how awareness and timely intervention can drastically reduce mortality rates.

Transitioning from talks to action, the event inspired participants to rethink how small, consistent health steps can make a big difference.

Street Play That Stirred Emotions

To make the message resonate deeply, BSc Nursing students performed a nukkad natak (street play) at the OPD Foyer. Through drama and emotion, they explained the importance of early detection, regular screening, and self-examination.

Their performance highlighted a crucial point — while technology and treatment options are improving, awareness remains the strongest medicine.

Doctors Urge Women to Stay Alert and Informed

Speaking to the crowd, Brig. Dr. Raju Agarwal urged women to adopt healthier lifestyles, undergo regular check-ups, and talk openly about their health.He emphasized that awareness is not just information — it’s empowerment. “Early diagnosis saves lives,” he said, calling on everyone to spread the message in their communities.

Transitioning from awareness to action, his words struck a chord with participants who pledged to encourage screening within their families.

The Rising Challenge: Why Awareness Matters More Than Ever

According to Dr. Pritanjali Singh, breast cancer continues to be the most common cancer among women globally. Citing GLOBOCAN 2022 data, she shared alarming numbers — 22.96 lakh cases worldwide, with 1.92 lakh in India.“Every four minutes, a new patient is diagnosed. Every eight minutes, one loses her life,” she said.However, she stressed that most deaths are preventable through early detection, regular screening, and continuous public education.

These statistics underline why events like AIIMS Patna’s Pink Walk are not just symbolic—they’re essential.

💗 A Step Toward Change

AIIMS Patna’s initiative is more than an awareness drive; it’s a collective commitment to save lives. Through collaboration between medical professionals, students, and the public, the Pink Walk reinforces that prevention begins with awareness and healing begins with conversation.

title: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan Visits Bihar, Pays Tribute to Jayaprakash Narayan
summary: When History Met Humanity: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan’s Heartfelt Visit to Sitab Diara In the serene village of Sitab Diara, where the Ganga gently flows past memories of freedom and hope, Vice
content:
When History Met Humanity: Vice President CP Radhakrishnan’s Heartfelt Visit to Sitab Diara

In the serene village of Sitab Diara, where the Ganga gently flows past memories of freedom and hope, Vice President Dr. CP Radhakrishnan paid a warm tribute to Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan (JP) on his birth anniversary.It was a day that blended remembrance, dialogue, and genuine human connection — marking the first-ever visit by a sitting Vice President to JP’s birthplace in Saran, Bihar.

A Visit Filled with Respect and Reflection

Amid the quiet rustle of the morning breeze, the Vice President garlanded JP’s statue and spent time reflecting on the reformer’s ideals of honesty, simplicity, and service to humanity.Rather than a formal event, it felt like a homecoming — a moment where respect met emotion.

During his 45-minute stay, Dr. Radhakrishnan interacted with villagers, listened to their thoughts, and assured them that their voices matter. Concerns about education, healthcare, and local development were shared openly, turning the occasion into a meaningful conversation rather than a ceremonial visit.

Listening to the People, Honoring a Legacy

One elderly villager, a follower of JP’s movement, shared his difficulties with receiving his pension. The Vice President responded with care, promising to forward the issue to the concerned authorities.Moments like these highlighted not just administration, but empathy — the kind of connection that Jayaprakash Narayan himself believed in.

The visit also included a gathering at the Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan Smriti Bhavan, where locals from across the region came together to remember the visionary whose ideas of justice and equality continue to inspire generations.

Remembering the Spirit of Jayaprakash Narayan

Born on October 11, 1902, JP remains one of Bihar’s most respected sons — a thinker who chose simplicity over comfort, people over politics.His journey from Sitab Diara to the national stage was rooted in one belief — that true leadership begins with listening.

From his daring escape from Hazaribagh Jail to his work for rural upliftment, JP’s story reminds us that progress isn’t just about power or policy — it’s about compassion, courage, and collective growth.

A Message That Still Echoes

Vice President CP Radhakrishnan’s visit wasn’t only about paying tribute; it was about reconnecting with values that define India’s moral strength.Sitab Diara stood still for a while that day — not in silence, but in pride, as villagers and visitors came together to celebrate the enduring spirit of a man who believed in people more than politics.

Bihar Government Launches 10-Day Training Program

The Bihar Government has launched a 10-day training program in Patna to equip local masons with earthquake-resistant construction skills. The initiative aims to strengthen disaster-resilient infrastructure across the state.

The program is organized by the Bihar State Disaster Management Authority (BSDMA) in collaboration with Astrik Computers India Pvt Ltd and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).

Objectives of the Program

The Bihar Government’s training program focuses on:

Developing technical skills for earthquake-resilient construction. Reducing the vulnerability of buildings in seismic zones. Creating a workforce that can support safe and sustainable construction across Bihar.

Creating a workforce that can support safe and sustainable construction across Bihar.

Priyanshu Ranjan Upadhyay Ankit Kumar Saurabh Kumar Deepu Kumar

Priyanshu Ranjan Upadhyay

Bihar lies in seismic zones IV and V, making it highly prone to earthquakes. Many older buildings lack proper structural safety. The Bihar Government’s initiative ensures that masons learn practical skills to construct safer structures.

This effort not only protects communities but also provides employment opportunities for skilled masons trained in disaster-resilient construction.

Broader Goals and Impact

The program is part of a broader government push to develop a disaster-ready workforce in Bihar. By training masons in earthquake-resistant techniques, the initiative strengthens both local construction standards and long-term community safety.

PM Modi Inaugurates Bihar’s First Skill University, 4,000 Youth Begin Their Career Journey!

Bihar’s youth just received a game-changing opportunity! On October 4, 2025, Prime Minister @narendramodi inaugurated the Bharat Ratna Jananayak Karpuri Thakur Skill University, a historic step in skill-based education and employment in the state.

Bihar’s Leap into Skill-Based Education

The university will revolutionize vocational training and employment opportunities. It will offer technical and vocational education, while promoting entrepreneurship, research, and innovation. This initiative complements Bihar’s Saat Nischay Part 1 and 2 schemes and helps youth compete nationally and internationally.

Moreover, the university will affiliate with various skill institutes, conduct exams, and confer degrees. These steps will equip Bihar’s youth with skills needed in today’s competitive job market.

4,000 Youth Receive Appointment Letters

At the same time, 4,000 candidates selected by the Labour Resources Department received appointment letters at Bapu Sabhagar, Patna. The government aims to connect 1 crore youth with jobs and self-employment opportunities in the next five years.

Ministers including Health Minister Mangal Pandey and Labour Resources Minister Santosh Kumar Singh emphasized that Bihar is creating new employment pathways. Additionally, a high-level committee will soon draft a five-year jobs policy for the state.

Leadership and Vision Behind the Initiative

The inauguration featured Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, Deputy CM Samrat Chaudhary, and senior state ministers including Union Minister Vijay Kumar Sinha. University leaders, such as Vice Chancellor Deepak Anand and Registrar Rajesh Bharti, actively participated in the launch.

A senior official said, “The university and today’s appointment letters reflect our commitment to building a skilled, self-reliant, and progressive Bihar.” This initiative demonstrates Bihar’s ambition to become a hub for skilled talent.

A Transformational Step for Bihar’s Youth

The university opens doors for thousands of youth to enter the workforce confidently. By merging education, skills, and employment, Bihar bridges the gap between potential and opportunity. Furthermore, structured skill development sets an example for other states in India.

Bihar Government Approves 3% DA Hike

Ahead of the festive season, the Bihar government announced a 3% increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for state employees and pensioners. This increase, effective July 1, 2025, raises the DA from 55% to 58%.

The cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, approved this step to provide financial relief to over 10 lakh people. The decision covers both government employees and pensioners, easing pressure from rising costs.

Relief for Employees and Pensioners

Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, who handles finance, described the hike as a “festival gift” for employees and pensioners.

The increase benefits over 5 lakh employees and 6 lakh pensioners. Moreover, it is expected to support household spending during Diwali and Chhath festivals.

Financial Implications

This DA hike will cost the state exchequer approximately ₹918 crore in the current fiscal year. Therefore, the government demonstrates its commitment to supporting employees and pensioners.

Additionally, this measure will help families manage daily expenses more comfortably.

Scholarships for School Students Doubled

The Bihar government also doubled scholarships for students from Class 1 to Class 8:

Classes 1–4: ₹1,200 annually (up from ₹600) Classes 5–6: ₹2,400 annually (up from ₹1,200) Classes 7–8: ₹3,600 annually (up from ₹1,800)

title: 57 new Kendriya Vidyalayas to be opened, most of them in Bihar
summary: Bihar Leads the Way! 57 New Kendriya Vidyalayas Approved, 19 Coming to Bihar Education in India just received a massive push — and Bihar is at the forefront. The Cabinet Committee on
content:
Education in India just received a massive push — and Bihar is at the forefront. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved the establishment of 57 new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) across 17 states and Union Territories. Remarkably, 19 of these will be in Bihar, making it the state with the largest share.

Why Bihar Gets the Maximum Share

Bihar is witnessing a rapid rise in central government employees. Consequently, the demand for quality education for their children has surged. KVs are expanding aggressively in Bihar, aiming to meet this growing need.

Moreover, Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan emphasized that these schools will serve aspirational districts, Left-Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areas, and hilly regions. Therefore, children in underserved communities will finally access quality education.

In addition, this expansion brings opportunity, hope, and progress. For thousands of children in Bihar, these schools will open doors to a brighter future.

What Makes These KVs Special?

These schools will cover Balvatika (pre-primary) to Class 12 and align with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. Specifically:

50 schools will receive sponsorship from state governments and UT administrations. 7 schools will be sponsored by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

50 schools will receive sponsorship from state governments and UT administrations.

7 schools will be sponsored by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

Furthermore, the Ministry of Education estimates that the project will cost ₹5,862.55 crore over nine years, including capital and operational expenses.

As a result, children will benefit from high-quality infrastructure and modern learning facilities, while states gain new opportunities for education-driven development.

Impact on Students and Jobs

Currently, 1,288 KVs operate across India, including branches in Moscow, Kathmandu, and Tehran, serving over 13.62 lakh students.

With the 57 new KVs:

Around 86,640 students will gain access to quality education. Nearly 4,617 permanent teaching jobs will be created. Children of central government employees will receive uniform standards of education nationwide.

Around 86,640 students will gain access to quality education.

Nearly 4,617 permanent teaching jobs will be created.

Children of central government employees will receive uniform standards of education nationwide.

Importantly, this approval comes after the government sanctioned 85 new KVs in December 2024. Thus, the recent expansion addresses rising demand while ensuring pan-India reach.

A New Dawn for Bihar’s Education

For Bihar, this marks a historic milestone. With 19 new KVs, many families in underserved districts will finally enjoy high-quality, affordable education. Additionally, the schools will nurture children from foundational years, preparing them for competitive exams and global opportunities.

This move is not merely policy — it reflects a promise to Bihar’s youth. Education, access, and opportunity are now closer than ever.
