title: Patna gears up for Dussehra 2025 with an 80-foot Ravana effigy : Know Traffic Plan & Rules for Dussehra 2025
summary: Patna on High Alert: 80-Foot Ravana Effigy, Strict Traffic Plan & Massive Security at Gandhi Maidan Patna is buzzing with excitement as the city prepares for Vijayadashami at Gandhi Maidan. This year’s
content:
Patna is buzzing with excitement as the city prepares for Vijayadashami at Gandhi Maidan. This year’s Ravana Dahan will feature an 80-foot Ravana effigy, effigies of Meghnath and Kumbhakarna, and strict traffic and security measures. Thousands are expected to attend, so the administration has unveiled a comprehensive plan to manage the crowd effectively.

Heightened Security Measures

Preparations are in full swing. On Monday, Divisional Commissioner Dr. Chandrashekhar Singh and Inspector General of Police Jitendra Rana reviewed the arrangements and instructed local officials to maintain order. They emphasized that Gandhi Maidan will operate as a fixed-venue, fixed-time celebration.

The administration divided Gandhi Maidan into four sectors, each monitored by an Additional District Magistrate and a Deputy Superintendent of Police. In total, 103 magistrates will actively manage 49 locations. Furthermore, three Quick Response Teams will assist in emergencies.

The security setup includes:

128 CCTV cameras 10 watchtowers with Civil Defence staff 34 light towers, 136 LED metal lights, 229 pole lights, and 15 high-mast lights

128 CCTV cameras

10 watchtowers with Civil Defence staff

34 light towers, 136 LED metal lights, 229 pole lights, and 15 high-mast lights

Meanwhile, police bike squads will patrol continuously. Visitors must enter through gates 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, and 12, while media personnel will use gate 13. Vehicles cannot enter the Maidan. Additionally, nine ambulances with medical teams will stay ready for emergencies.

Spectacular Effigies and Fireworks

The festival promises a breathtaking display. At 5:45 p.m., the 80-foot Ravana effigy, designed by Agra-based artists, will ignite. Beside it, a 75-foot Meghnath and a 70-foot Kumbhakarna will burn simultaneously. Additionally, an elaborate fireworks show will light up the evening sky.

Consequently, families will enjoy a vivid celebration of the triumph of good over evil. Therefore, attending early and following safety rules will enhance the experience.

Strict Traffic Rules Around Gandhi Maidan

From 11 a.m. on October 2, Patna Police will enforce strict traffic regulations. Authorities closed several roads near Gandhi Maidan and allowed only VIP or pass-holding vehicles at select points.

Key restrictions include:

No entry from Bhattacharya Square, Dakbungalow Square, and JP Golambar Emergency vehicles can use the JP Golambar–Children’s Park stretch No parking from JP Golambar to Dakbungalow Square, Dakbungalow Square to Patna Junction, and Ramgulam Chowk to Exhibition Road

No entry from Bhattacharya Square, Dakbungalow Square, and JP Golambar

Emergency vehicles can use the JP Golambar–Children’s Park stretch

No parking from JP Golambar to Dakbungalow Square, Dakbungalow Square to Patna Junction, and Ramgulam Chowk to Exhibition Road

Furthermore, authorities designated parking zones for pass-holders at:AN Sinha Institute, Gyan Bhawan, SBI Campus, JP Ganga Path, Mauryalok Campus, Veerchand Patel Path, and Harding Road.

Citizens’ Cooperation is Key

Traffic police, home guards, and flying squads will actively monitor all critical points. Authorities have already set up barricades and checkpoints. CCTV cameras will continue recording throughout the day.

Officials urged citizens to avoid unnecessary vehicle movement near Gandhi Maidan. Instead, people should use public transport or walk to the venue. Consequently, these efforts will ensure a safe and enjoyable celebration for all.

title: Top 5 Districts Leading the Bihar’s Economic Boom— The Names Will Shock You
summary: Bihar’s Growth Story: Top 5 Fastest-Growing Districts Redefining the State’s Future Bihar is changing, and the transformation is visible even from space. 🌍 A recent satellite-based study reveals how the glow of
content:
Bihar is changing, and the transformation is visible even from space. 🌍 A recent satellite-based study reveals how the glow of Bihar’s nights reflects its rising economy. The study shows which districts are leading in growth and which emerging ones are turning into new economic centers.

Patna Leads, But Others Are Catching Up

It is no surprise that Patna tops the list. The capital has always been a hub for education, government, and trade. However, the study shows that Vaishali, Muzaffarpur, Gaya, and Begusarai are also rapidly expanding their economic activities.These districts have shown remarkable growth in night-time illumination between 2017 and 2023, proving the spread of industries, markets, and public infrastructure.

Emerging Economic Hubs on the Rise

Interestingly, the report also highlights Arwal, Jehanabad, Jamui, Banka, and Madhubani as upcoming growth centers. Once considered backward, these districts now show major shifts in trade, agriculture, and services.For example, the glow of night lights in Arwal and Jehanabad grew from just 50 sq. km to 389 sq. km in six years. This signals better electricity access, more businesses, and rising living standards.

More Than Agriculture: A Diverse Growth Pattern

Bihar’s story is no longer limited to farming. These districts are embracing e-commerce, healthcare, and startups alongside traditional businesses. The Asian Development Research Institute (ADRI), in partnership with the Bihar Industries Department, carried out this research. Their findings highlight that growth is becoming multi-sectoral and not restricted to one industry.Such diversity ensures stronger resilience and opportunities for youth across the state.

The Return of Old Industrial Giants

Districts like Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga, and Bhagalpur were once known for their industries. Over time, they lost prominence. But now, they are re-emerging as industrial and commercial hubs. With better infrastructure and rising investments, these areas could once again power Bihar’s economy.

President Droupadi Murmu Performs Pind Daan in Gaya Ji During Pitru Paksha Mela

Faith and leadership came together when President Droupadi Murmu visited the sacred city of Gaya Ji in Bihar. Known as a global center of ancestral rituals, the holy land witnessed her performing pind daan for her forefathers.

She arrived early in the morning and walked straight into the temple premises. Bihar Governor Arif Mohammad Khan joined her during this sacred visit, adding further dignity to the occasion.

Rituals of Pitru Paksha

The President remained inside the temple for more than two hours. During this time, she performed every ritual with devotion. Priests guided her through the offerings, chants, and sacred rites of pind daan, which believers say ensure peace for departed souls.

Importantly, the visit coincided with the ongoing Pitru Paksha Mela. Every year, lakhs of devotees reach Gaya Ji during this period. By joining them, President Murmu highlighted the living bond between traditions and modern leadership.

Faith Meets Leadership

After completing the rituals, she offered prayers with folded hands. Soon after, she departed for New Delhi on a special aircraft. However, her time in Gaya Ji sent a strong message. Even the nation’s highest authority bows before the values of culture and faith.

For Bihar, her presence was more than a formal visit. It became an acknowledgment of its spiritual identity and deep traditions. Over centuries, kings, saints, and leaders have performed pind daan in this city. Now, President Murmu has become part of that historic lineage.

title: Bihar govt makes Student Credit Card loans interest-free
summary: Big Relief for Students: Bihar Makes Student Credit Card Loans Interest-Free Patna, Bihar: Imagine studying without worrying about loan interest piling up. For thousands of students in Bihar, that dream is now
content:
Patna, Bihar: Imagine studying without worrying about loan interest piling up. For thousands of students in Bihar, that dream is now a reality.

The Bihar government has announced that all Student Credit Card (SCC) loans under the Saat Nischay Yojana are now completely interest-free. This step is designed to reduce financial stress for students and give them the freedom to focus entirely on their education.

What’s New in the Student Credit Card Scheme?

Earlier, education loans carried interest—4% for general students, and a reduced 1% for female, differently-abled, and transgender students. Now, every student will pay zero interest.

Repayment terms have also been made easier:

Loans up to ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 5 years to 7 years. Loans above ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 7 years to 10 years.

Loans up to ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 5 years to 7 years.

Loans above ₹2 lakh: Repayment period extended from 7 years to 10 years.

This means students can pay back in smaller installments over a longer time, easing financial pressure.

Why This Change Matters for Students

The rising cost of higher education often stops students from pursuing their dreams. By removing interest and giving more time to repay, Bihar is helping young learners continue their studies without fear of debt.

The SCC scheme already allowed loans of up to ₹4 lakh for higher education. With the new update, it is now even more accessible and supportive for students from every background.

A Step Toward Accessible Education

This move is more than a policy—it’s a message that education should not come with financial barriers. Students now have the freedom to choose courses and colleges with confidence. They can focus on learning, gaining skills, and building careers, instead of worrying about repayment stress.

In the long run, this support can open doors for more engineers, doctors, researchers, and professionals from Bihar, shaping a brighter future for the state and its youth.

The Road Ahead for Bihar’s Students

Interest-free loans and flexible repayment terms will inspire many more students to step into higher education. It means better opportunities, more graduates, and stronger representation of Bihar’s talent in India and beyond.

title: Bihar Idea Festival 2025: 25,000 Startup Ideas and BIIPP 2025 Put Bihar on India’s Industrial Map
summary: Bihar Idea Festival 2025: 25,000 Startup Dreams, Bold Policies, and the Promise of a New Bihar A Wave of Ideas from the Heart of Bihar What happens when a state unlocks the
content:
A Wave of Ideas from the Heart of Bihar

What happens when a state unlocks the entrepreneurial spirit of its youth? Bihar just answered that with the Bihar Idea Festival 2025, where an astounding 25,000 startup ideas poured in from every district. The finale, held at Bapu Sabhagar, Patna, was not just a celebration of ideas but also a showcase of Bihar’s bold leap into industrial growth, global exports, and inclusive entrepreneurship.

Big Announcements That Redefine Bihar’s Future

The event concluded with the launch of Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Package (BIIPP) 2025, the One Block One Product (OBOP) initiative, and the opening of the APEDA regional office in Patna. Together, these moves position Bihar as a rising hub for investment, industry, and export.

Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal praised Bihar’s new policies and called BIIPP 2025 one of the most liberal packages in India. With incentives such as free land, 300% SGST reimbursement, and strong startup support, Bihar is clearly preparing for a transformational journey. He also announced the Centre’s approval of four new industrial parks and reaffirmed plans for the 3,000-acre industrial township in Gaya.

A Changed Bihar: From Small Budgets to Big Dreams

Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary highlighted the state’s progress. Bihar’s budget once stood at ₹6,000 crore. Today, it has risen to ₹37,000 crore, fueling jobs and industrial growth. He urged the Centre to consider new industrial corridors to meet the aspirations of Bihar’s 14 crore population.

M. Kumar Singh, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industries Department, shared key details of BIIPP 2025. Job-creating industries can now access up to 25 acres of free land, while others get 50% concession on BIADA land rates. Add to that capital subsidies, export promotion incentives, and green industry support—and Bihar’s industrial ecosystem suddenly looks more attractive than ever.

One Block One Product: Taking Bihar’s Treasures to the World

The OBOP initiative is extending the successful ODOP model to all 534 blocks. From Bhagalpur silk to Muzaffarpur’s Shahi litchi, from Darbhanga makhana to Madhubani paintings, each block will now receive branding, packaging, certification, and global market access.

The Chief Minister Entrepreneur Scheme and Bihar Micro Entrepreneur Scheme were also highlighted, which have already supported more than 43,500 entrepreneurs—many scaling their businesses beyond ₹1 crore turnover.

25,000 Ideas, 5 Winning Innovations

Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO of YourStory, who spearheaded the outreach, shared how the festival exceeded expectations. “We set out to collect 10,000 ideas. Bihar’s youth gave us 25,000, even from schoolchildren in Classes 9 and 10. This shows Bihar’s hidden entrepreneurial energy,” she said.

The top five winning ideas showcased the creativity of Bihar’s youth:

An AI-powered legal system Waste management solutions Smokeless gas innovations Drone technology applications Portable wastewater treatment systems

An AI-powered legal system

Waste management solutions

Smokeless gas innovations

Drone technology applications

Portable wastewater treatment systems

These innovations prove that Bihar’s startup ecosystem is not just about numbers—it is about relevance, scale, and solving real-world problems.

Building a Complete Industrial Ecosystem

Industries Minister Nitish Mishra underlined Bihar’s readiness to become a serious player in India’s industrial map. From special economic zones to land banks, and from OBOP support to startup funding, Bihar is creating a full-fledged growth ecosystem.

With export promotion offices, industrial parks, and large-scale policy incentives, Bihar is no longer looking at government jobs as the only aspiration. Instead, the youth are now preparing to create enterprises that will power the next wave of growth.

The Road Ahead

The Bihar Idea Festival has not only celebrated innovation but has also redefined Bihar’s industrial vision. With bold policies, youth-driven entrepreneurship, and global export potential, Bihar is signaling to the world: this is a state ready for take-off.

title: No coach, no fancy gear: Bihar labourer finishes as runner-up in Spiti marathon
summary: From Khagaria to Kunzum La: Bihar Labourer Rohit Kumar’s Marathon Dream Towards the 2028 Olympics A Runner With No Coach, No Gear—Just Grit “No coach. No fancy gear. Just raw resolve.” That’s
content:
A Runner With No Coach, No Gear—Just Grit

“No coach. No fancy gear. Just raw resolve.” That’s how the Army described Rohit Kumar, a 32-year-old daily wage labourer from Khagaria, Bihar, who recently stunned the nation with his marathon achievement.

Working at a construction site in Delhi, Rohit spends his mornings not on rest but on the road. While most wake up at sunrise, he laces his worn-out shoes at 4:30 am. His dream? To one day wear the Indian jersey at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics in the Triathlon.

Spiti Marathon Glory Against All Odds

At the Surya Spiti Challenge 2025, Rohit competed in the brutal 77 km Kunzum La–Kaza Ultra. With icy winds, thin air, and steep climbs, this race isn’t for the faint-hearted. Yet Rohit crossed the finish line second, clocking 7 hours and 44 minutes.

The Army’s Uttar Bharat shared his story on X, writing:“He doesn’t chase records or sponsorships. He runs to survive. His finish line was not just a medal—it was dignity, hope, and a step closer to his Olympic dream.”

This wasn’t his first big achievement. In fact, Rohit has participated in more than 100 marathons, often averaging five races in a single month. Now, he says he focuses on quality over quantity.

Life Between Labour and Long Runs

Balancing life as a construction worker with the demands of training isn’t easy. Yet Rohit chooses sacrifice over excuses. Out of his modest ₹30,000 monthly income, he spends nearly ₹20,000 on his diet and running equipment.

Inspired by marathon greats from London, New York, and Tokyo, he began training in 2020 without a coach. Every run is self-taught, every step powered by sheer will. And when asked about his next step, he simply smiles: “I will get another podium finish.”

The Road Ahead: Arunachal and Beyond

After Spiti, Rohit has already received an invitation to another high-altitude marathon in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. The Indian Army has promised to take care of his travel, food, and lodging. He hopes this will be another podium finish that pushes him closer to his Olympic dream.

For Rohit, the journey is about more than medals. He runs for those who remain unseen—the countless daily wage workers who shoulder heavy burdens yet carry silent dreams in their hearts.

title: Bihar Women Commission launches Online Complaint Filing from 19th September
summary: अब घर बैठे मिले न्याय: Bihar Women Commission launches Online Complaint Filing from 19th September When justice knocks on your door instead of you knocking on its gate, change feels real. Bihar
content:
When justice knocks on your door instead of you knocking on its gate, change feels real. Bihar Women Commission has taken such a bold step. Starting 19th September, women across Bihar can register their complaints online without traveling to Patna.

This initiative, launched on the 24th Foundation Day of the Commission, is a historic stride toward making justice faster, fairer, and more accessible.

A Digital Lifeline for Women in Bihar

Till now, women had to reach the Commission office in Patna to file complaints. For those from remote villages, the journey often meant financial stress and emotional struggle.

Now, with the new online process, this hardship ends. Women can simply visit the official website, fill in a digital form, and submit their grievance. This not only saves time and money but also ensures that no woman feels left behind.

How Will the Online Complaint Process Work?

The Commission Chairperson, Apsara Mishra, explained the process clearly. The system is designed to be as easy as filling out a student admission form online.

Women need to enter their name, address, mobile number, and case details. They must provide the details of the person against whom they are filing. A separate column lets them select the complaint category—domestic violence, dowry harassment, sexual harassment, property dispute, or others.

Women need to enter their name, address, mobile number, and case details.

They must provide the details of the person against whom they are filing.

A separate column lets them select the complaint category—domestic violence, dowry harassment, sexual harassment, property dispute, or others.

Finally, the woman can complete the process with a digital signature. This ensures authenticity and prevents fake or incomplete submissions.

Faster Action, Transparent Monitoring

The moment a complaint is filed online, the technical cell and relevant officers get notified. After a preliminary review, the complainant receives updates about the next steps.

Moreover, the digital process allows the Commission to maintain a record of every case. This enhances transparency, helps in monitoring, and ensures better follow-up.

With this, women no longer have to spend days traveling or waiting. Instead, their concerns get attention more quickly and efficiently.

Why This Change Matters Now

For years, women from distant districts faced difficulty reaching Patna. Some never came forward due to cost, time, or hesitation. This digital leap removes those barriers.

It also aligns with the Digital India mission, making governance inclusive and tech-driven. Importantly, it shows that Bihar is ready to empower women with practical solutions, not just promises.

A Step Dedicated to Women’s Dignity

Chairperson Apsara Mishra stated, “Many women hesitated to travel far and narrate their pain. Now, they can raise their voice from home. Our goal is that no woman should wander for justice.”

This reflects a deep commitment to accessibility and dignity. Justice, after all, should not be a privilege—it must be a right that reaches every doorstep.

title: Bihar Hikes Stipend for 1.2 Lakh Anganwadi Workers & Helpers
summary: Big Relief for 1.2 Lakh Families: Bihar Hikes Stipend for Anganwadi Workers and Helpers They are the unsung heroes of every village—guiding children, supporting mothers, and making sure nutrition and care reach
content:
Big Relief for 1.2 Lakh Families: Bihar Hikes Stipend for Anganwadi Workers and Helpers

They are the unsung heroes of every village—guiding children, supporting mothers, and making sure nutrition and care reach every home. Their hard work now receives long-awaited recognition.

Stipend Hike Announced for Anganwadi Workers

On September 8, 2025, the state government announced a significant stipend hike for anganwadi workers and helpers. More than 1.20 lakh sevikas and sahayikas across Bihar will directly benefit from this decision.

Under the new update, anganwadi workers (sevika) will now receive ₹9,000 per month, increased from the earlier ₹7,000. Similarly, anganwadi helpers (sahayika) will now get ₹4,500, up from ₹4,000.

Why This Matters for Bihar’s Communities

Anganwadi workers are the backbone of community health and nutrition programs. They serve as frontline caregivers, helping children receive early education, proper nourishment, and guidance for mothers during pregnancy.

With this stipend increase, their contribution is finally being acknowledged in a meaningful way. The hike is not just financial support—it is also a gesture of respect for their tireless service.

Anganwadi’s Role in Welfare and Change

From monitoring child nutrition to spreading awareness about health, anganwadis play a transformative role in Bihar’s villages. Over the years, they have been instrumental in shaping healthier communities and creating awareness at the grassroots level.

Now, with better financial security, workers are expected to feel more valued, which could strengthen their impact on families across the state.

title: NIRF 2025 Ranking :IIT Patna Jumps in National Ranking
summary: IIT Patna’s Remarkable Leap: From Rank 73 to 36 in National Rankings When was the last time Bihar made national headlines for academic excellence? Today, it’s IIT Patna stealing the spotlight with
content:
When was the last time Bihar made national headlines for academic excellence? Today, it’s IIT Patna stealing the spotlight with a massive leap in the Ministry of Education’s National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2025. The institute has climbed from 73rd place last year to 36th place in the overall category—a jump that showcases Bihar’s growing academic power.

What Makes the NIRF Ranking Important?

The NIRF rankings, released annually by the Ministry of Education, are one of the most trusted benchmarks for higher education in India. This year’s list spans across 17 categories, including a newly added one on Sustainable Development Goals (SDG).

These categories highlight diverse strengths—from engineering and medicine to research and innovation. For students and parents, they serve as a transparent guide to choosing the right institution. For colleges and universities, they create healthy competition to improve teaching, research, and overall learning experience.

India’s Top Performers in 2025

The top spots remain unchanged. IIT Madras continues to hold the first position, followed by the Indian Institute of Science (Bengaluru), IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi, IIT Kanpur, and IIT Kharagpur.

However, below the top six, some notable shifts took place:

IIT Roorkee climbed from eighth to seventh. AIIMS Delhi slipped to eighth. Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) jumped to ninth. Banaras Hindu University (BHU) entered the top 10. IIT Guwahati dropped out of the top 10, moving to eleventh place.

IIT Roorkee climbed from eighth to seventh.

AIIMS Delhi slipped to eighth.

Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) jumped to ninth.

Banaras Hindu University (BHU) entered the top 10.

IIT Guwahati dropped out of the top 10, moving to eleventh place.

IIT Patna’s Rise: A Game-Changer for Bihar

Among all these changes, IIT Patna’s rise stands out the most. From 73rd to 36th, the institute has recorded one of the biggest jumps in NIRF history. This achievement highlights:

Stronger teaching standards. Improved research quality. A growing academic environment that encourages innovation.

Stronger teaching standards.

Improved research quality.

A growing academic environment that encourages innovation.

For Bihar, this is more than a number. It reflects the state’s capacity to nurture excellence in higher education. As the only IIT in Bihar, Patna’s performance strengthens eastern India’s academic ecosystem and inspires thousands of young students.

Why This Matters for Students and Parents

Education is no longer just about classrooms and degrees. With NIRF expanding its categories to include skill universities, open universities, state public universities, and now SDGs, the focus is shifting towards holistic learning.

content:
“Bihar’s Bold Step: Now File Corruption Complaints from Home as Vigilance Bureau Reaches Your Doorstep”

Fighting Corruption, One Home at a Time

Imagine raising your voice against corruption without traveling miles to Patna. For thousands of people across Bihar, this is no longer a dream. The Vigilance Investigation Bureau (निगरानी अन्वेषण ब्यूरो) has launched a new initiative to directly reach citizens in their districts and villages.

This effort aims to remove the barrier of distance and fear. Instead of waiting for complaints in Patna, officials will now visit regions where victims live.

Officers Meeting Victims in Person

Senior officers from the Vigilance Bureau will meet corruption victims face-to-face. They will listen, record complaints, and begin immediate follow-up action. This campaign will gradually cover almost all districts of Bihar.

The journey starts in Bhagalpur and Purnia, where officers will stay between 21 and 23 August 2025. During these days, citizens can meet them at the Bhagalpur Vigilance Bureau office, the DM office, and the nearby Combined Building. Officials will also travel across local areas to make the process easier.

No More Patna Trips for Complaints

For years, victims had to travel to Patna just to register corruption cases. Many faced hardship, extra expenses, and delays. According to Vigilance DG Jitendra Singh Gangwar, this step ensures relief from that struggle.

Now, instead of people coming to the Bureau, the Bureau is coming to them. It’s a small but powerful shift, designed to restore trust in the system.

Direct Contact for Complaints

Citizens can not only meet officers in person but also call dedicated numbers. The Vigilance Bureau has released 9939044222 and 6207099360 for this purpose. By doing so, they are creating multiple pathways for people to raise their voices.

Why This Matters for Bihar

Corruption has long been a roadblock for Bihar’s progress. By reaching villages and districts, this initiative ensures that ordinary citizens feel heard. It also shows that accountability is no longer limited to big cities.

The move could inspire more people to come forward, making transparency stronger at the grassroots.

title: Bihar Govt & IIT Delhi Launch AI Training for Engineers in Bridge Design and Monitoring
summary: Bihar Engineers to Get AI Training at IIT Delhi: A New Era in Smart Bridge Design When was the last time you looked at a bridge and thought about the science behind
content:
When was the last time you looked at a bridge and thought about the science behind its strength? Starting this September 2025, Bihar is rewriting that story by bringing artificial intelligence, drones, and real-time data into the world of bridge design and safety. And leading this revolution is IIT Delhi, in collaboration with the Bihar government.

Bihar Engineers Step Into the Future

More than 100 government engineers will undergo a six-month certification programme at IIT Delhi. The training will teach them to use AI-driven tools, drones, and sensors for bridge monitoring, design, and maintenance.

This initiative falls under the Bihar State Bridge Management and Maintenance Policy, 2025. Unlike earlier systems, the policy now makes drone-based inspections mandatory for all state-maintained bridges. The shift aims to ensure accuracy, speed, and cost-effectiveness in infrastructure safety.

What Will Engineers Learn?

The new curriculum is not just about theory. It focuses on hands-on technology. Some of the modules include:

AI & Machine Learning: Computing Bridge Health Index (BHI) scores from drone and sensor data. Real-Time Monitoring: Using strain gauges and tilt meters to detect stress points instantly. Smart Planning: Applying Maintenance Priority Index (MPI) models to decide which bridges need urgent repairs.

AI & Machine Learning: Computing Bridge Health Index (BHI) scores from drone and sensor data.

Real-Time Monitoring: Using strain gauges and tilt meters to detect stress points instantly.

Smart Planning: Applying Maintenance Priority Index (MPI) models to decide which bridges need urgent repairs.

These modules promise to make Bihar engineers self-reliant and skilled in future-ready bridge technology.

A Dedicated Bridge Design Cell

Alongside training, the government will set up a Bridge Design Cell under Bihar Rajya Pul Nirman Nigam Limited (BRPNNL). This in-house facility will design bridges, culverts, and retaining walls for Bihar.

Officials estimate that this single step could save over ₹65 crore annually by reducing reliance on external consultants. It also means fewer project delays and faster delivery of safe infrastructure to the public.

Expanding Technical Partnerships

The Bihar government is also in talks with the Indian Academy of Highway Engineers (IAHE) to introduce additional specialized training. Together, these collaborations aim to build a pool of highly skilled bridge engineers who can lead projects not only in Bihar but across India.

Policy That Brings Change

Under the Bihar State Bridge Management and Maintenance Policy, 2025, drone inspections are now compulsory. This approach will help prioritize repairs with real-time accuracy and reduce risks caused by weak structures.

Bihar’s Public Works Minister Nitin Nabin emphasized, “The future of infrastructure lies in technology and self-reliance.” His statement underlines Bihar’s commitment to both innovation and safety.

Rollout Plan for 2025-26

Deployment begins in the financial year 2025-26. In the first phase, 85 bridges will undergo real-time monitoring. Both IIT Delhi and IIT Patna will jointly audit these bridges.

With this move, Bihar isn’t just maintaining old structures. It is building a resilient, tech-powered, and safer bridge network for its people.

title: Bihar’s Freedom Fighters and War Heroes Who Changed India’s Destiny
summary: From Valour to Victory: Bihar’s Sons and Daughters Who Changed India’s Destiny Bihar – Where Courage Meets History When you speak of India’s freedom and military glory, Bihar’s name shines like a
content:
From Valour to Victory: Bihar’s Sons and Daughters Who Changed India’s Destiny

Bihar – Where Courage Meets History

When you speak of India’s freedom and military glory, Bihar’s name shines like a blazing torch. This land has produced fearless men and women who stood against oppression, fought on battlefields, and inspired generations. From the grit of Veer Kunwar Singh to the unyielding spirit of Usha Mehta, Bihar’s legacy is carved in courage and sacrifice.

Veer Kunwar Singh – The Lion of 1857

In the Revolt of 1857, when most leaders were crushed by the British, Kunwar Singh of Jagdishpur rose like a storm. At the age of 80, he led fierce battles, outsmarted colonial forces, and became a living symbol of resistance. Even while injured, he cut his wounded arm and offered it to the Ganga, choosing dignity over defeat. His bravery echoes through history as one of India’s first war cries for independence.

Rajendra Prasad – The First President of India

Dr. Rajendra Prasad, born in Siwan, was more than a leader; he was the soul of India’s Constitution. From joining Mahatma Gandhi’s movements to steering the nation as its first President, his vision for a united India remains unmatched. His simplicity and integrity continue to guide leaders even today.

Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan – The Voice of the People

Known as JP, he was the man who shook the foundations of political dictatorship during the Emergency in 1975. Born in Sitab Diara, his call for “Total Revolution” mobilised millions. His fearless stance for democracy became a lesson in civic courage for every Indian.

War Heroes Who Defended the Nation

Bihar’s courage didn’t stop with freedom. In modern times, warriors like Captain Manoj Kumar Pandey (Param Vir Chakra awardee) and Major Chandrakant Singh have defended India’s borders with unmatched loyalty. Their sacrifice is a reminder that bravery is Bihar’s eternal language.

Women Who Defied Chains

Bihar’s history is also adorned with heroines like Shanti Devi, who carried messages for revolutionaries, and Phoolan Devi, who rose from oppression to challenge injustice. Their stories prove that courage wears many faces – and gender is never a barrier to resistance.

Bihar’s Spirit Lives On

These icons are not just names in history books; they are the reason Bihar stands proud. Their spirit runs in the veins of every young dreamer from this soil. And as Bihar continues to produce leaders, thinkers, and warriors, the world sees a state that refuses to bow down.

summary: Patna Kicks Off ‘Har Din Har Gali’ Drive to Keep Every Street Clean A Daily Dose of Cleanliness for Patna Imagine waking up to spotless streets every single day. That’s the vision
content:
Patna Kicks Off ‘Har Din Har Gali’ Drive to Keep Every Street Clean

A Daily Dose of Cleanliness for Patna

Imagine waking up to spotless streets every single day. That’s the vision Patna Municipal Corporation has rolled out with its new campaign — ‘Har Din Har Gali’. The goal is simple but powerful: make every street in the city cleaner, safer, and healthier.

Launched on August 14, 2025, the drive focuses on 100% door-to-door garbage collection, mosquito control, and daily road cleaning. The Municipal Commissioner, Animesh Kumar Parashar, shared that this mission is about more than tidiness — it’s about protecting public health and boosting Patna’s rank in the Swachh Survekshan survey.

Morning Checks, Real-Time Reports

This campaign comes with strict monitoring. Every day from 7 AM, ward nodal officers will inspect their areas. By 2 PM, they’ll send detailed cleanliness reports to headquarters.

Public places will also see lime and bleaching powder spraying to prevent infections. Additionally, anti-larva spraying and fogging will be done regularly to keep mosquito-borne diseases at bay.

Zones Under Strong Leadership

To make things run smoother, the city has been divided into six zones under two leaders. Ashish Kumar will oversee Patliputra, Kankarbagh, and Patna City. Rajan Sinha will handle Nutan Rajdhani, Bankipur, and Azimabad.

These officials will not only inspect work daily but also coordinate closely with ward officers. Their hands-on approach is expected to speed up problem-solving and improve results.

Residents at the Heart of the Mission

The Municipal Corporation knows that a city can only stay clean if its residents take part. That’s why they are urging people to cooperate with garbage collectors, avoid littering, and keep areas around their homes clean.

With this collective effort, Patna is aiming for more than just neat streets. It’s about creating a city that reflects pride, health, and responsibility in every lane.

title: Patna Launches Weekly ‘No Horn Day’
summary: “No Horn Sundays in Patna: Silence Speaks Louder Than Honks!” When the city slows its noise, hearts listen better. Patna has taken a bold step towards peace with the launch of a
content:
“No Horn Sundays in Patna: Silence Speaks Louder Than Honks!”

When the city slows its noise, hearts listen better. Patna has taken a bold step towards peace with the launch of a weekly ‘No Horn Day’. Every Sunday, until October 2, the streets will echo less with blaring horns and more with mindful silence, thanks to the initiative by the Bihar State Pollution Control Board (BSPCB).

A City’s Pledge for Peace

The campaign urges drivers to avoid unnecessary honking, especially in quiet zones like hospitals, courts, schools, and within 100 metres of sensitive spots including the secretariat, legislative assembly, Raj Bhavan, and the city’s biological park.

Officials are clear: reducing noise is not just about comfort—it’s about health. Studies show that constant exposure to loud sounds increases stress, disturbs sleep, and even affects heart health. By embracing silence, residents can literally breathe easier.

Awareness Across Patna’s Four Zones

To make the change visible, the BSPCB has divided Patna into four zones. Their teams will visit key spots, talking to motorists and locals about why noise matters. Volunteers and officials will hand out awareness leaflets, while traffic police will encourage drivers to keep their hands off the horn—unless absolutely necessary.

Many citizens already see the difference. “It’s refreshing,” says Sunita, a teacher from Kankarbagh. “For the first time, I could hear birds chirping during my Sunday walk.”

Loudspeakers Under the Scanner Too

The BSPCB has also reminded residents about existing restrictions on loudspeakers, DJs, and public address systems. Without special permission, these cannot be used between 10 pm and 6 am. Anyone breaking the rules risks penalties under Section 15 of the Environment Protection Act, 1986. Equipment may even be seized under the Noise Pollution Rules, 2000.

The message is clear—Patna is ready to reclaim its soundscape. Less honking, fewer late-night loudspeakers, and more moments of calm can turn the city into a healthier, happier place.

summary: Chandrayaan Dreams in Village Streets: ISRO’s ‘Space on Wheels’ Sparks Curiosity in Bihar’s Young Minds! From Patna to Purnia—ISRO’s Space on Wheels Rolls Through Bihar with Wonder “What does space smell like?”That

Chandrayaan Dreams in Village Streets: ISRO’s ‘Space on Wheels’ Sparks Curiosity in Bihar’s Young Minds!

From Patna to Purnia—ISRO’s Space on Wheels Rolls Through Bihar with Wonder

“What does space smell like?”That was the question a curious student from a government school in rural Bihar asked while stepping into ISRO’s traveling marvel—the “Space on Wheels” mobile exhibition.

This wasn’t just a van. It was a galaxy on wheels, carrying satellites, rocket models, and interactive displays to villages, towns, and schools across 20 different locations in Bihar. For over 30,000 students and residents, it was their first glimpse into the world of rockets, moon missions, and beyond.

What is ISRO’s Space on Wheels?

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) launched the Space on Wheels initiative to make space science approachable and thrilling for everyone. Instead of waiting for students to reach museums or science centers, ISRO brings the universe to them—on wheels.

These mobile exhibitions travel across India, featuring interactive models, animated videos, real-time demonstrations, and hands-on experiments. The goal? Spark scientific curiosity, especially among children in rural and underserved regions.

Bihar’s Young Minds Light Up

In Bihar, the mobile exhibition became a festival of science. Children gathered in schoolyards, anganwadis, and open grounds, eager to explore the stars—often for the very first time.

Here’s what made Bihar’s leg of the tour unique:

Diverse Reach: Covered schools in districts like Muzaffarpur, Nalanda, Gaya, and Bhagalpur. Massive Participation: Reached over 30,000 individuals from different walks of life. Inclusive Learning: Rural students got to interact with space models, mission simulations, and multilingual guides. Teacher Support: Educators were provided resources to carry forward space learning in classrooms.

Diverse Reach: Covered schools in districts like Muzaffarpur, Nalanda, Gaya, and Bhagalpur.

Massive Participation: Reached over 30,000 individuals from different walks of life.

Inclusive Learning: Rural students got to interact with space models, mission simulations, and multilingual guides.

Teacher Support: Educators were provided resources to carry forward space learning in classrooms.

The Power of Curiosity and Connection

This initiative wasn’t just educational—it was emotional.For many students in Bihar, especially in rural belts, science often feels like a distant concept. But through Space on Wheels, it came rolling into their lives—real, touchable, and thrilling.

Children watched videos of Chandrayaan and Aditya L1, touched miniature PSLV models, and saw how satellites help forecast floods in their own regions.

They didn’t just learn facts—they dreamed.Some started saying they wanted to work at ISRO. Others asked how to build a rocket.

That’s not just outreach. That’s transformation.

Why This Matters for Bihar’s Future

Bihar has always been home to brilliant minds. But initiatives like this help nurture that brilliance from a young age, especially in places where resources are limited.

With a growing population of curious, tech-driven youth, Bihar is poised to become a contributor—not just a consumer—of India’s space future. ISRO’s efforts through programs like Space on Wheels could be the foundation of that journey.

title: Khadi Training centres in Bihar Empowers Rural Women
summary: “Thread by Thread, She Rises: How Khadi is Stitching a New Future for Bihar’s Women” ✨ From Fabric to Freedom: Bihar’s Women Weave a New Tomorrow with Khadi Kapda nahi, zindagi badal
content:
“Thread by Thread, She Rises: How Khadi is Stitching a New Future for Bihar’s Women”

✨ From Fabric to Freedom: Bihar’s Women Weave a New Tomorrow with Khadi

Kapda nahi, zindagi badal raha hai Khadi!

Khadi is no longer just about spinning wheels and simplicity. In Bihar, it’s turning into a powerful movement — a tool of empowerment, identity, and income for rural women. With every stitch and every thread, women across the state are stepping into roles of dignity, self-reliance, and leadership.

Khadi Training: Where Skill Meets Self-Reliance

Supported by the Bihar Government, Khadi training centres are now active in multiple districts. These are not ordinary workshops — they are transformation hubs where women learn stitching, embroidery, knitting, soap-making, incense stick production, and detergent creation.

Unlike traditional training that only scratches the surface, these programs go deeper. Women learn design thinking, fabric selection, and also how to package and market their products effectively. This isn’t just about skill; it’s about sustainability.

In 2024–25 alone, 59 training programmes were conducted. Over 950 women and 550 men joined these initiatives, with many women now earning through Khadi centres or launching their own businesses.

Role Models in the Making: Women at the Forefront

From small villages to block-level towns, women are rewriting their stories. Earlier limited by financial dependence or social norms, these women are now earning, saving, and inspiring. What’s more? They’re becoming symbols of change in their communities.

Their stories aren’t just personal wins — they reflect a larger shift in rural Bihar’s gender dynamics.

“Khadi is not just cloth anymore. It is culture, creativity, and confidence,” said Industry Minister Nitish Mishra.

“Khadi is not just cloth anymore. It is culture, creativity, and confidence,” said Industry Minister Nitish Mishra.

He also announced the launch of Khadi malls in all divisions and a digital push to sell local products online. His tagline — “Khadi for Fashion, Khadi for Nation, Khadi for Transformation” — is quickly gaining traction.

Fashion Meets Livelihood: Khadi Goes Glam

Gone are the days when Khadi was only associated with dull fabrics. Now, it’s turning fashionable. Designers are blending Khadi with trendy cuts and modern silhouettes, making it appealing for the younger generation.

This pivot toward fashion is also opening new career paths for trained women — from tailors and artisans to micro-entrepreneurs and local fashion influencers.

And it’s not just about income. With every saree stitched and every soap sold, women are gaining confidence, purpose, and recognition.

A Grassroots Revolution Backed by Vision

This isn’t a one-off story. It’s a grassroots revolution backed by policy, purpose, and people. With more centres being planned and digital tools being introduced, Khadi is on track to become a pillar of rural economic development.

These women are not waiting for opportunities — they are creating them.

Bihar goes digital with empathy — From grievance redressal to healthcare, tech is now touching lives.

A Revolution Rooted in Responsibility

In a bold move that reflects Bihar’s shift towards transparent, tech-driven governance, the state government launched a suite of digital reforms on July 25, 2025. The flagship launch includes the RTPS Online Appeal & Review Portal, a user-first platform that empowers every citizen to raise their voice against delays or denial of government services.

Held at the Secretariat Meeting Hall in Patna, the launch was spearheaded by the Chief Secretary of Bihar, who called this moment “a promise delivered digitally.” With just a few clicks, citizens can now appeal or review their grievances under the Bihar Right to Public Services Act, 2011. No more long queues, no more paperwork. It’s time for real-time justice.

RTPS Portal – A Public Right Made Clickable

Built to reduce bureaucratic delays, the portal offers:

Paperless application & grievance process Digital signature verification Real-time dashboards for tracking

title: Bihar Passes Historic Bill : 4 Lakh Aid for Gig Workers’ Welfare
summary: ₹4 Lakh Aid for Delivery Workers’ Families: Bihar’s Landmark Step to Protect Gig Workers” The Ground Beneath Their Wheels Just Got Safer Every time a delivery partner speeds through traffic, they’re not
content:
₹4 Lakh Aid for Delivery Workers’ Families: Bihar’s Landmark Step to Protect Gig Workers”

The Ground Beneath Their Wheels Just Got Safer

Every time a delivery partner speeds through traffic, they’re not just racing against time—they’re risking their life for our convenience. In a historic move, Bihar has taken a people-first step to support gig workers like delivery boys, riders, and temporary laborers by passing the Platform-Based Workers’ Welfare Bill 2025. This isn’t just policy—it’s a message that every life matters, even when it’s on two wheels.

Gig Workers in Bihar to Get ₹2-4 Lakh Compensation for Death

The bill passed in the monsoon session of the Bihar Assembly promises direct financial aid to gig workers and their families.Here’s what it brings to the table:

₹4 lakh aid in case of accidental death ₹2 lakh for natural death Disability support ranging from ₹74,000 to ₹2.5 lakh for 40-60% disability Hospitalisation aid of ₹5,400 (under 1 week) and ₹16,000 (more than 1 week) Maternity benefit for women gig workers Unique ID for every registered gig worker to access welfare schemes

₹4 lakh aid in case of accidental death

₹2 lakh for natural death

Disability support ranging from ₹74,000 to ₹2.5 lakh for 40-60% disability

Hospitalisation aid of ₹5,400 (under 1 week) and ₹16,000 (more than 1 week)

Maternity benefit for women gig workers

Unique ID for every registered gig worker to access welfare schemes

Moreover, the government has mandated all platform companies and aggregators to register their gig workforce within 60 days. This will ensure they’re brought under the safety net.

Welfare Board for Gig Workers – A First for Bihar

To ensure implementation, a Welfare Board will be formed. It will be chaired by the Labour Resource Department Minister and include platform company representatives. This board will address grievances, release aid, and monitor worker safety.

Gig workers will now hold a government-recognised identity and can directly benefit from official schemes—something that was unthinkable just a few years ago.

Longer Overtime Limits – But Only with Consent

Another key development: the state has amended the Factories Act 1948, increasing the overtime cap from 75 to 144 hours per quarter. However, written consent from workers is now mandatory. This allows workers to earn more without being exploited.

Other Important Bills Passed in This Session

While the focus remained on gig workers, the Bihar Assembly also passed bills that will impact various sectors:

Karpoori Thakur Skill University Bill 2025: Bihar’s first dedicated skill university Bihar Shops & Establishment Amendment Bill 2025: Reforms for working conditions Animal Breeding Regulation Bill 2025: Stronger rules in livestock sector Bihar Agricultural University Amendment Bill 2025: Recruitments now through BPSC, BTSC, BSSC

Karpoori Thakur Skill University Bill 2025: Bihar’s first dedicated skill university

Bihar Shops & Establishment Amendment Bill 2025: Reforms for working conditions

Animal Breeding Regulation Bill 2025: Stronger rules in livestock sector

Bihar Agricultural University Amendment Bill 2025: Recruitments now through BPSC, BTSC, BSSC

Each bill aims to streamline processes, strengthen governance, and boost employment opportunities.

Why This Matters

India’s gig economy is booming, but its backbone—the workers—are often invisible, unprotected, and unaccounted for. With this bill, Bihar becomes one of the first Indian states to formally recognise their rights and risks.

And while we aren’t naming political figures, this is a people-first move that deserves attention beyond party lines.

title: Patna Nursing Students Lead Organ Donation Awareness
summary: “One Pledge, Many Lives: Patna’s Nursing Students Show the Way for Organ Donation” Most people think of nurses as silent workers in white coats. But on a recent afternoon at IGIMS Patna,
content:
“One Pledge, Many Lives: Patna’s Nursing Students Show the Way for Organ Donation”

Most people think of nurses as silent workers in white coats. But on a recent afternoon at IGIMS Patna, these young students were anything but silent.

They were creating art. They were absorbing life-saving knowledge. More importantly, they were stepping up for something that can save lives long after ours end—organ donation.

Why This Campaign Mattered

This wasn’t just a classroom session. It was part of the national ‘Jeevan Sanjivani’ campaign, designed to spark awareness about organ donation.

At the College of Nursing, IGIMS Patna, students joined hands with doctors and faculty over two powerful days. Together, they made the topic personal, emotional, and urgent.

A Competition That Touched Hearts

On day one, the college organised a poster-making competition. It was open to both BSc Nursing and GNM students. Rather than treating it as another college event, students gave it their all.

Some painted stories of loss and rebirth. Others created bold messages:“Don’t carry your organs to heaven—heaven knows we need them here.”

The creativity was compelling. However, the emotions behind each poster were what made them unforgettable.Winners will be honoured on Organ Donation Day, but in truth, every participant contributed to a larger cause.

Turning Facts Into Purpose

The second day moved the conversation forward. A special lecture was organised to help students understand how organ donation works and why it matters.

Dr. Anuja Daniel, Principal of the College of Nursing, opened the session. She reminded students that awareness drives like these are essential—not just for learning, but for leadership.

Moreover, she explained that nurses play a crucial role in organ donation—from identifying potential donors to counselling families. In her words, Bihar has the potential to lead, just like other progressive states, if it commits to spreading this message.

Encouraging the Next Generation of Changemakers

Following that, Dr. Manish Mandal, Chairman of SOTO, spoke directly to the students.He talked about how organ donation is managed under the National Organ Transplant Program, and how science is progressing every single day.

Unlike typical lectures, his words were direct. He urged students not just to listen but to research, write, and initiate conversations. He believed young minds can build new momentum for the movement.

Making the Pledge Real

Then came IEC Consultant Ekta, who explained the process in simple terms.

Anyone above 18, she said, can pledge their organs online. To do so, one simply needs to visit www.notto.abdm.gov.in. She clarified doubts, broke myths, and gave students a clear call to action.

Several students decided to pledge that very moment. Others promised to discuss it at home. Clearly, something shifted in the room that day.

Closing a Chapter, Opening a Mission

The event closed with a warm vote of thanks from Dr. Rupashree Dasgupta, Vice Principal of the College. Faculty members, SOTO’s transplant coordinator Jaspal Singh, and program assistant Seema Kumari were also present.

While the formal program ended, the sense of responsibility stayed behind. The students left with more than certificates or applause—they left with conviction.

Now, they are ready to be ambassadors of change, not just in hospitals, but in society.

Don’t Wait to Make a Difference

If you’re over 18, take a moment. Visit www.notto.abdm.gov.in. One pledge can save up to eight lives.

Government’s Vision: From Industry to Education

Bihar’s Education Department has announced a powerful plan. Begusarai, known for its industrial base, will now be shaped into a major educational hub.

S. Siddharth, the Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) of the Education Department, recently shared this vision while visiting Begusarai. He made it clear—Bihar no longer wants to rely only on Patna for quality education.

He explained that the location gives Begusarai a strategic edge. Since it lies close to Patna, it can serve students from across the region. That’s why the government is now aiming to balance both industrial growth and intellectual development.

“Begusarai must become an academic role model,” said Siddharth.

“Begusarai must become an academic role model,” said Siddharth.

Closing the Gap Between Private and Government Schools

Siddharth emphasized that the focus is not just on building schools but also on ensuring equal access to quality education.

Instead of relying solely on private institutions, the state is:

Appointing more teachers in government schools. Improving basic infrastructure rapidly. Introducing modern facilities, similar to private schools.

Improving basic infrastructure rapidly.

Introducing modern facilities, similar to private schools.

Because of these actions, government schools in Begusarai are now seeing real transformation. The teaching staff shortage has been addressed. More importantly, the gap in learning environments between private and public schools is narrowing.

Siddharth stated that in the coming years, students from government schools won’t feel left behind. He also called for collaboration between both sectors, encouraging joint efforts to improve teaching standards.

Why Begusarai? Location, Potential, and Growth

So, what makes Begusarai the right choice?

Geographical Advantage: It’s near Patna, offering easy access and wider connectivity. Industrial Reputation: With Barauni nearby, it already holds economic importance. Untapped Academic Potential: Despite having institutions, the education sector hasn’t reached its full strength.

content:
छुट्टी का प्लान बना लिया? These Trains from Bihar Will Take You Straight to Hill Heaven!

Bihar Train News: Explore India’s Hill Stations This Summer—Boarding Starts Right Here!

Who says summer in Bihar has to be hot and hectic? What if we told you that a cool breeze, snow-capped peaks, and pine-scented adventures are just one train ride away? Yes, you read that right. Several long-distance trains passing through Bihar can take you directly to India’s most stunning hill stations, making your summer break nothing short of magical!

Whether you’re craving the serenity of Himalayan valleys or the bustling charm of hill towns, Bihar has got you covered—by rail.

Why This Matters for You

Many Biharis are currently planning trips to beat the heat. While air travel sounds tempting, nothing beats the affordability, comfort, and scenic routes offered by Indian Railways.

Now, here’s a handpicked list of trains passing through Bihar that can take you straight to some of the most popular hill station gateways in India.

Trains from Bihar That Take You to the Hills

1. Lohit Express (Train No. 15651) – For the Scenic North

This Mail Express connects Guwahati (Assam) to Jammu Tawi (J&K). It passes through Bihar and is your perfect ride to explore hill stations around Jammu, such as Patnitop, Sanasar, and Bhaderwah.

✅ Pro Tip: Book early. Jammu-bound trains fill fast in summer!

2. Howrah-Amritsar Mail (Train No. 13005) – Himachal Beckons

Board this train and get down at Amritsar. From here, you’re just a short ride away from famous hill destinations like Dalhousie, Kangra, Chamba, Mandi, and Dharamshala.

➡️ Bonus: You also get to explore the Golden Temple and Wagah Border on the way!

3. Saryu Yamuna Express (Train No. 14649) – Touch the Foothills

This express train connects Jaynagar (Bihar) to Amritsar Junction. From Jalandhar or Amritsar, you’re close to picturesque towns like Nurpur, Amb, and Palampur.

✨ A great option if you’re traveling from North Bihar!

4. Upasana Express (Train No. 12328) – Uttarakhand’s Gateway

Running between Dehradun and Howrah, this train is a gem. Get down at Dehradun, the entry point to gems like Mussoorie, Rishikesh, and Dhanaulti.

🌄 Perfect for families and solo travelers alike.

5. Bagh Express (Train No. 13019) – For the Lovers of Kumaon

This Mail Express takes you from Howrah to Kathgodam (via Bihar). Kathgodam is the nearest railhead to Nainital, Mukteshwar, and Ranikhet.

🍃 Did someone say boating in Naini Lake?

6. Archana Express (Train No. 12355) – Patna to Jammu

This weekly train runs between Patna and Jammu Tawi, making it an ideal option for people from Bihar wanting to explore North India’s hidden hill treasures.

💡 Jammu’s proximity to unexplored hills makes this route a must-try!

All Aboard the Adventure Train

With these options, your dream hill vacation is just a ticket away. And the best part? You don’t need to change multiple trains or break the bank. Indian Railways brings the mountains to your doorstep—starting right here in Bihar.

Ready to trade the plains for the peaks?

content:
“Ek Bihari, NASA Pe Bhaari!” – Meet the 17-Year-Old from Samastipur Who Entered NASA’s Cybersecurity Hall of Fame

What happens when a child’s love for video games turns into a mission to secure the internet?

Ram Jee Raj, a 17-year-old from Samastipur, Bihar, has taken the global tech world by storm. The self-taught ethical hacker recently entered the NASA Hackers’ Hall of Fame after uncovering a major vulnerability on NASA’s official website.

From Gaming Curiosity to Global Cyber Fame

Ram’s story began like many childhoods in India—with games. However, unlike others, he looked behind the screen.“What makes a game run?” he wondered.

This simple question launched him into the world of coding, game development, and web design. Eventually, he stumbled across hacking-related films. That curiosity soon grew into a passion for ethical hacking—all self-taught from his small town.

By the age of 11, Ram was already writing code. He began scanning websites for flaws and responsibly reporting them. Over the years, he has quietly contributed to the digital safety of hundreds of platforms, all without formal education in cybersecurity.

The Email That Shook NASA

In the early hours of May 14, 2024, Ram emailed NASA with a report about a critical flaw on their website.

Within just five days, on May 19, the agency confirmed the vulnerability, resolved it, and officially acknowledged Ram’s findings.Just like that, a teenager from a lesser-known town in Bihar earned a spot in one of the world’s most prestigious security circles:🚀 The NASA Cyber Security Hall of Fame.

The son of Rinkesh Kumar, Ram represents a powerful truth—you don’t need a Silicon Valley zip code to be a world-class tech innovator.

AI Dreams Rooted in Real Problems

Ram is not stopping at hacking.

In fact, he’s already ventured into AI-driven innovation. He has built platforms like:

MedVed AI – to assist in affordable healthcare FarmEye – to enhance smart agriculture YUVA Sathi – to empower rural youth with digital education

MedVed AI – to assist in affordable healthcare

FarmEye – to enhance smart agriculture

YUVA Sathi – to empower rural youth with digital education

These projects have earned him national and global recognition, including listings in the USA Book of World Records and multiple innovation awards.

Currently, he’s developing an AI-based startup to revolutionize farming.“My aim is simple,” he says.“If one farmer can take care of five cows today, I want to help him manage five hundred—with tech.”

Bihar’s Youth Are Not Behind — They Just Need the Mic

content:
A New Door Opens for Bihar’s Brightest Legal Minds!

In a major win for legal education in Bihar, Chanakya National Law University (CNLU), Patna, has signed a groundbreaking Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the University of Leicester, UK. This strategic tie-up marks a turning point for students aspiring to pursue LLM abroad—bringing global opportunities one step closer to home.

Global Gateway: LLM Made Accessible for CNLU Graduates

Signed by Prof. Faizan Mustafa, Vice-Chancellor of CNLU, and Daniel Greco, Global Partnerships Manager at Leicester University, the MoU will allow CNLU graduates a direct pathway into Leicester’s prestigious LLM program.

What’s even better? CNLU students will enjoy a 30% fee concession, and those from economically weaker backgrounds can apply for additional scholarships offered by the University of Leicester.

This agreement isn’t just about access—it’s about empowerment. With UK-based exposure, Bihar’s legal scholars will now get to sharpen their expertise on an international stage.

Beyond LLM: More Collaborations on the Horizon

Prof. Mustafa shared his vision for more such collaborations. According to him, this MoU is just the beginning. He’s confident that similar tie-ups with top international universities are on the way. These global links will enable joint research, academic exchange, and long-term collaboration—setting the tone for CNLU’s transformation into a global academic hub.

Such partnerships signal a mindset shift: Bihar’s institutions are now thinking beyond borders. And rightly so.

Why Now? A Changing Landscape for Legal Education in India

The timing couldn’t be more perfect. With the Supreme Court’s revival of the three-year rule for judicial service eligibility, law graduates now have renewed options. CNLU, keeping pace with this change, is stepping up to ensure its students don’t just compete—but lead.

In addition to this international collaboration, CNLU has launched a Civil Services Academy. This initiative offers personalised coaching for students aiming for UPSC and state civil services. It’s a two-pronged strategy: while some students will explore global degrees, others will receive full support to crack top national exams.

Bihar’s Legal Youth: On the Verge of a Global Leap

This MoU represents more than just an agreement between two institutions. It’s a statement. A clear message that students from Bihar can dream big, aim global, and achieve beyond boundaries.

So whether you’re a law graduate in Patna, or a parent hoping for your child’s brighter future—this news is for you. And it’s just the beginning.

title: Bihar’s village where every home raises a soldier
summary: A Village Raised by the Army – And Still Raising Soldiers In Bihar’s Katihar district, there’s a village that beats to the sound of patriotism. Welcome to Mirzapur — a name less
content:
A Village Raised by the Army – And Still Raising Soldiers

In Bihar’s Katihar district, there’s a village that beats to the sound of patriotism. Welcome to Mirzapur — a name less heard, but never forgotten. Here, from nearly every household, a young soldier marches out to serve the nation.

Over 300 youth from this village are currently in the Indian Army. That’s not just a number. It’s a living, breathing legacy stretching over six decades.

A Legacy Forged in Service and Sacrifice

Why is Mirzapur so different? It’s not just geography — it’s mindset.

Perched beside the sacred Ganga river, the village doesn’t have lavish roads or modern gyms. But it has what many places lack — purpose. And that purpose is clear: serve India, wear the uniform, protect the borders.

In the words of a local, “Every child here dreams of joining the Army. It’s not a choice; it’s our identity.”

Even the Kargil War saw sons of Mirzapur martyred. Two bravehearts from this very soil never returned, and yet, their sacrifice only made the village stronger. That’s what makes it more than just a place — it’s a monument of courage.

Training Without Fear, Dreaming Without Limits

Walk into the lanes of Mirzapur, and you’ll find a different kind of classroom. Here, open fields are boot camps. Morning jogs replace morning assemblies. Elders — mostly veterans — train the young, passing down drills like heirlooms.

Despite facing lack of infrastructure, the passion never fades. In fact, it grows.

What’s even more inspiring? This cycle of service continues generation after generation. Sons follow fathers. Younger brothers salute elder ones. Some families have three men in uniform — all serving in different units across India.

Imagine a city in Bihar with the swanky feel of Gurugram, the planning of Noida, and the heart of Mithila — yes, it’s happening, and it’s happening in Darbhanga!

In a bold and progressive move, the Bihar government is all set to develop a Mega Township in Darbhanga’s Laheriasarai, transforming this historic region into a modern, self-sufficient city.

From Legacy to Modernity: Why Darbhanga?

Darbhanga isn’t just any town — it’s Bihar’s first planned city, born from the post-1934 earthquake vision. And now, it’s back in the spotlight. Minister Jivesh Mishra, during a site visit, announced that this township will be modeled on Gurugram’s urban development blueprint — featuring skyscrapers, parks, shopping malls, schools, and sports grounds.

Thanks to existing infrastructure like AIIMS, an airport, a planetarium, and an IT Park, Darbhanga is the perfect launchpad for Bihar’s mega urban revolution.

“We are identifying three prime locations for Phase 1,” said Minister Mishra. “These will include schools, sports fields, and lush parks. A detailed map and masterplan are already in progress.”

“We are identifying three prime locations for Phase 1,” said Minister Mishra. “These will include schools, sports fields, and lush parks. A detailed map and masterplan are already in progress.”

RE-4 Exam Before August: Bihar to Recruit 1.6 Lakh Teachers, Major Overhaul Underway

Bihar is on the edge of its biggest teacher recruitment yet — and the timeline is tight.In a decisive move, the Bihar government has set the stage for the BPSC TRE-4 exam before August 2025, aiming to recruit over 1.6 lakh teachers. This isn’t just a hiring spree; it’s a bold step toward reforming the education landscape.

The Countdown Has Begun: August 10 Is the Key Deadline

Education Minister Sunil Kumar clearly stated that all transfers and postings will wrap up by August 10. Immediately afterward, the BPSC TRE-4 recruitment exam will begin.

This round will open up more than 1.6 lakh teaching positions across primary and secondary schools. The urgency reflects the government’s clear priority — fix the teacher gap without delay.

Recruitment Beyond Numbers: Special Educators and Compassionate Hiring

The upcoming drive doesn’t stop at regular teachers. The state is also focusing on inclusivity.

➡️ 7,279 special educators will be recruited for children with disabilities.➡️ 6,421 posts will be filled on compassionate grounds for eligible candidates.

Districts are already mapping schools and identifying requirements. Additionally, the BPSC will handle these processes under newly framed recruitment rules, making the system fairer and faster.

Faster Exams, Stronger Systems

The Education Minister emphasized a commitment to punctuality and transparency. Therefore, exams like Sakshamta Pariksha (Competency Test) and Special Educator Exams will follow strict schedules.

Moreover, internal reviews are ensuring smooth coordination between the BPSC, education department, and district offices. These checks aim to maintain accountability throughout the recruitment.

Reforms that Support Women and Improve Infrastructure

During a review meeting, the government issued immediate instructions to resolve maternity leave issues faced by women teachers. This is a long-awaited relief for thousands of educators.

Additionally, the state is:

Constructing boundary walls for girls’ hostels. Digitizing land records of schools and colleges. Building a land bank to support school expansion.

Constructing boundary walls for girls’ hostels.

Digitizing land records of schools and colleges.

Building a land bank to support school expansion.

Each move aims to create safer, more efficient learning spaces across Bihar.

Continuous Teacher Training from 2025

Starting this year, all teachers will undergo training twice a year at DIET (District Institute of Education and Training). These sessions will last one week each and will focus on new teaching techniques.

This isn’t just a routine exercise. It reflects Bihar’s serious commitment to skill development and classroom impact.

Meanwhile, a statewide hostel improvement campaign is also being launched to fix unsafe and unhygienic conditions.

Political Collaboration: MLAs to Get Faster Responses

Recognizing the importance of public representatives, the Education Department will now act promptly on MLA and MLC recommendations. This change will reduce delays and ensure that genuine demands get addressed without red tape.

It marks a shift toward more people-centric governance.

A Fresh Era for Education in Bihar

From fast-track recruitments to women-friendly policies, from better infrastructure to improved training — Bihar’s education system is finally undergoing a massive reset.

This isn’t a plan for the future. It’s happening now, and the results could reshape thousands of schools.

title: No More Traffic Jam at Patna Junction – Smart Vending Zone Plan in Action
summary: Patna’s Big Breakthrough: No More Traffic Chaos Near Junction! Nagar Nigam’s New Vending Zone Plan in Motion A New Dawn for Patna Junction – Traffic Relief is Finally Coming Tired of the
content:
Patna’s Big Breakthrough: No More Traffic Chaos Near Junction! Nagar Nigam’s New Vending Zone Plan in Motion

A New Dawn for Patna Junction – Traffic Relief is Finally Coming

Tired of the endless jam and chaos around Patna Junction? You’re not alone. But here’s the good news—Patna is on the brink of a major transformation. The days of squeezing through congested lanes and breathing foul air near the city’s busiest railway zone might soon be over.

The Patna Municipal Corporation, under the leadership of Municipal Commissioner Animesh Kumar Parashar, has rolled out a strategic plan to solve the junction mess once and for all.

What’s the Plan? A Modern Vending Zone to the Rescue

The main focus is the Kabadi Market, located just opposite Buddha Smriti Multi-Level Parking. This cluttered, unregulated space is set to be replaced by a modern vending zone. Inspired by the successful model in Kadamkuan’s Ward 38, this initiative will offer registered vendors a structured and hygienic place to operate.

A detailed land survey is already underway, with instructions given to map both existing municipal land and any additional land needed. The survey report is expected within a week.

Why Now? The High Court Steps In

This plan isn’t just proactive—it’s also responsive. The Patna High Court recently pulled up the administration for the relentless traffic jams and unbearable stench near the station. This judicial nudge has turned up the heat, and the Nagar Nigam is now moving with urgency.

The Vendor Story: 350+ Lives to Be Reshaped

Currently, over 350 vendors operate in the Patna Junction area, many without proper space or regulation. Despite repeated anti-encroachment drives, the issue persists. That’s because there has never been a long-term solution—until now.

By relocating and registering these vendors in a designated vending zone, the corporation aims to decongest footpaths and ease vehicular flow, all while safeguarding livelihoods.

Why It Matters: Linking to Smart City Goals

This isn’t an isolated move. Patna is part of the Smart City Mission, and under that banner, a Multi-Modal Hub and Subway System is already being developed near the junction. But these can only function efficiently if roadside encroachments are cleared and vendors are systematically accommodated.

Earlier, the Buddha Smriti Parking was considered for vendor relocation. However, that space will now serve as a designated auto parking zone, ensuring better last-mile connectivity.

Citywide Vision: More Zones on the Horizon

This isn’t a one-off fix. The municipal body has already approved four additional model vending zones in Wards 14, 30, 58, and 42. Now, Ward 28—home to the Kabadi Market—is next in line. The goal is to create a network of structured vending spaces across the city, each offering security, sanitation, and order.

💥 Change Is Here – And It’s Just the Beginning

From judicial pressure to administrative action, the momentum is real. With Commissioner Animesh Kumar Parashar leading the charge, this isn’t just about traffic—it’s about reclaiming public space, restoring order, and renewing faith in governance.

Patna Junction is more than a station—it’s a lifeline. And finally, it’s getting the structured ecosystem it deserves.

Bihar’s Sky Dreams Take Flight From Valmikinagar

Imagine watching a 19-seater aircraft soaring above the lush forests of West Champaran—because now, it’s no longer just a dream. Under the Central Government’s ambitious UDAN Scheme, Bihar is finally ready to add another feather to its aviation cap. The long-awaited approval for air service from Valmikinagar Airstrip, located in Bagaha Police District, is here. And this time, it’s real.

After years of anticipation, the runway is set. Small aircraft with 19 seats will soon connect this scenic region to the rest of the country. This is more than just news—it’s a leap in infrastructure, opportunity, and identity for Bihar.

What Is the UDAN Scheme and Why It Matters for Bihar?

UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) is a flagship initiative by the Government of India. Its goal? Make air travel affordable and accessible to underserved and unserved regions.

Thanks to this program, Valmikinagar has made it to the list under Bid Process Phase 5.2. And it’s not just about planes. It’s about progress.

Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu has confirmed the approval via an official letter addressed to Valmikinagar MP Sunil Kumar. The Ministry has recognized the site as fully suitable for small aircraft operations.

Boost to Tourism, Jobs, and Disaster Management

With this development, reaching the Valmiki Tiger Reserve will now be quicker and easier. Tourists will no longer need to brave long hours of road travel. This move is expected to give a significant boost to eco-tourism, local hospitality, and wildlife conservation awareness.

But the benefits don’t end there.

Local businesses will find new markets. Emergency services will become faster during natural disasters. Job opportunities in aviation and allied sectors will increase.

Emergency services will become faster during natural disasters.

Job opportunities in aviation and allied sectors will increase.

In short, a small airstrip is unlocking big potential.

Land Given, Sky Opened: The Role of State Government

The Bihar Government has played a pivotal role by providing land for the airstrip free of cost and without legal hurdles. Their proactive stance sent a clear message to the Centre—Bihar is ready for takeoff.

From airstrips to heliports and even water aerodromes, the central government is now keeping a close eye on aviation expansion in eastern India, with Valmikinagar becoming a focal point.

MP Sunil Kumar expressed deep gratitude to the Centre, calling it a “historic moment for West Champaran.” He rightly said that this move fulfills a decades-old dream of the local population.

From Regional Airstrip to National Conversation

This is not just about a new flight route. It’s about changing the narrative.

For far too long, Bihar’s story has been told in terms of struggle. But with news like this, the spotlight shifts—towards development, inclusion, and innovation. The people of Bihar have waited patiently, and now, their aspirations are ready to fly.

So, whether you’re a tourist, entrepreneur, or a student dreaming big—Valmikinagar might just be your new gateway.

content:
“Majboor Nahi, Majdoor Hain Hum” — The Real Truth About Bihar’s Migrants

Every year, lakhs of Biharis step out of their homes — not out of helplessness, but out of sheer determination.

They don’t leave Bihar because they have to.They leave because they want to work, to earn, and to uplift their families.Across India and beyond, they are silently shaping economies.

From Mumbai’s industries to construction sites in Dubai, and from food deliveries in Delhi to power plants in Gujarat — Biharis are everywhere.

Bihar: India’s Silent Workforce Hero

Let’s talk facts — because numbers speak volumes:

Bihar leads in the highest share of migration for work in India (Census 2011). Over half of all rural families in Bihar depend on remittance money. A migrant worker from Bihar sends back ₹26,020 annually — often the only source of income for the entire family. In Siwan and Gopalganj, remittance fuels 80% of the local economy, mostly from Gulf nations.
