In Siwan and Gopalganj, remittance fuels 80% of the local economy, mostly from Gulf nations.

Clearly, this isn’t a story of the helpless. It’s a story of grit, courage, and relentless hard work.

They Build India, But Still Go Unseen

Let’s pause and look around.

That new building rising in Bengaluru? A Bihari laid its foundation.That quick delivery you just received? A Bihari navigated narrow lanes to hand it to you.That road connecting two major towns? A Bihari worked overtime to get it done.

Still, many refer to them as “majboor.”This label couldn’t be further from the truth.

These are skilled, reliable, and dedicated workers. They are majdoors in the truest sense — powering India, brick by brick and street by street.

Why Should They Have to Leave Bihar to Be Valued?

India depends on their movement. But why should they move away for dignity?

What if we built Bihar for them?What if opportunity came home?

Imagine a Bihar with:

That Bihar is possible — if we invest in the right policies and platforms.

This Labour Day, let’s flip the script.

Let’s stop calling them helpless.Let’s start seeing them as the nation-builders they truly are.

It’s time we recognise their skills, sacrifices, and spirit.

As a result, users can stream live TV channels directly using a smart TV and the SkyPro app. It’s smooth, quick, and seamless.

title: Two-Day Training for Bihar BLOs by EC
summary: A New Chapter in Bihar’s Electoral Readiness “Chunav ka Bigul baj chuka hai!”Yes, the countdown has begun for Bihar’s Assembly Elections 2025, and the Election Commission of India is wasting no time.
content:
A New Chapter in Bihar’s Electoral Readiness

“Chunav ka Bigul baj chuka hai!”Yes, the countdown has begun for Bihar’s Assembly Elections 2025, and the Election Commission of India is wasting no time. In a powerful move, the EC launched an intensive two-day training and capacity-building programme for Booth Level Officers (BLOs) from Bihar. And this is not just routine—this is a masterclass in democracy management.

Held at the India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM), the event kicked off with the presence of two powerful names—Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioner Dr. Vivek Joshi. Their interaction set the tone for what’s being termed as one of the most focused training initiatives in recent times.

What’s the Big Deal About This Training?

Quite a lot, actually.

A total of 229 BLOs, along with 12 Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and 2 District Electoral Officers (DEOs) from Bihar, are being trained. That’s not all—a specialized session for the State Police Nodal Officer (SPNO) and other key Police Officers is also part of this packed programme.

The goal'o familiarize BLOs with their responsibilities under the electoral framework and make them tech-ready. The officers are getting hands-on experience with new IT applications that will help in maintaining error-free electoral rolls.

And the result of this training? These BLOs will become Assembly Level Master Trainers (ALMTs)—spreading their knowledge and enhancing the electoral machinery from the grassroots.

Why This Matters More Than Ever

With Bihar heading into crucial elections later this year, the pressure is high. But instead of relying on outdated methods, the EC is investing in smart systems and smarter people.

This session is part of Phase 1 of the physical training programmes and follows the training of over 555 BLOs from Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam. Additionally, 279 Booth Level Agents (BLA-1s) of major political parties in Bihar have also undergone training.

Such steps are ensuring that democracy is not just practiced—but perfected.

Policing the Process: Behind-the-Scenes Readiness

While the BLOs are being trained to ensure electoral accuracy, police officers are being empowered to safeguard the process.

From vulnerability assessments to deployment of CAPFs (Central Armed Police Forces), every aspect is being covered to ensure peaceful, fair elections. Special sessions are also dedicated to the Model Code of Conduct (MCC), ensuring that no line is crossed when the elections heat up.

The Bigger Picture

This isn’t just training—it’s an investment in trust and transparency. The Election Commission is making sure that when Bihar goes to the polls, every vote counts, every process is clean, and every officer is ready.

And it’s not just Bihar—this programme sets a benchmark for the rest of the nation too. A more trained BLO corps today means a stronger, more accountable democracy tomorrow.

From Weaving Dreams to Cracking JEE: 40 Students from Bihar’s IIT Village Rewrite Their Destiny in 2025

Bihar’s ‘IIT Village’ Patwa Toli Produces 40 JEE Main Qualifiers in 2025

Once known for its weaving looms, Patwa Toli in Bihar’s Gaya district is now making headlines for something else entirely—its bright, determined students. This year, over 40 students from the so-called ‘IIT Village’ have cleared the JEE Main 2025, transforming their modest beginnings into a springboard for national success.

Vriksha Sansthan: Nurturing Talent, One Dream at a Time

Among these successful aspirants, 28 are students of Vriksha Sansthan, a free coaching initiative founded and funded by former IITians. Since its inception in 2013, Vriksha has supported hundreds of students from underprivileged families, particularly those from the weaving community, with free coaching, study materials, and expert mentorship.

What sets Vriksha apart is its innovative library-based learning model. Instead of expensive coaching institutes, students learn through online sessions conducted by IIT alumni from Delhi and Mumbai. This remote teaching method has brought elite education to the doorstep of those who need it the most.

Meet the Top Achievers of 2025

This year’s top scorers from Patwa Toli include:

Sharanya – 99.64 percentile Alok – 97.7 percentile Shaurya – 97.53 percentile Yash Raj – 97.38 percentile Shubham – 96.7 percentile Pratik – 96.35 percentile Ketan – 96.00 percentile Nivas – 95.7 percentile Gaurika Yadav – 95.1 percentile Sagar Kumar – 94.8 percentile

All of them carry a common story—hard work, mentorship through Vriksha Sansthan, and a relentless drive to break the cycle of poverty.

A Legacy Born in 1991, Still Growing Strong

The story of Patwa Toli’s transformation began in 1991, when Jitendra Patwa became the first from the village to enter IIT. Now settled in the United States, he gives back through his NGO, ‘Vriksh We The Change’, which supports educational efforts in his hometown.

Since then, engineering has become more than just a career—it’s a village-wide aspiration. Every house now dreams of nurturing an IITian, and the statistics prove that this is no fantasy.

How Free Education is Empowering Families

“Some families just can’t afford to send their children outside for coaching,” says Dubeshwar Prasad, President of Vriksh Veda Chain. “That’s why we created a local system where students learn through libraries and online classes conducted by our seniors.”

The impact is visible. Even after Class 10, when most students in such villages drop out or join manual labor, these children are cracking India’s toughest exams.

From ‘Manchester of Bihar’ to ‘Village of IITians’

Patwa Toli was once called the ‘Manchester of Bihar’ for its flourishing textile trade. Now, it’s better known for producing engineers and doctors. The shift from thread to tech didn’t happen overnight. It was driven by a shared belief that education is the most powerful tool to transform lives.

Vriksha Sansthan continues to empower girls as well, opening doors that were once shut for them. More and more daughters of weavers are preparing for NEET and JEE, stepping out of traditional roles and into classrooms.

summary: Bihar’s First Vande Metro Gears Up for Launch! The Journey Will Now Feel Like an Experience Forget long, exhausting train rides—Bihar is all set to welcome its first Vande Metro, a high-speed,
content:
Bihar’s First Vande Metro Gears Up for Launch!

The Journey Will Now Feel Like an Experience

Forget long, exhausting train rides—Bihar is all set to welcome its first Vande Metro, a high-speed, next-gen intercity train designed to transform rail travel forever. Built using cutting-edge Indian Railways technology, this modern marvel is already running successfully in Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat. Now, it’s Bihar’s turn to ride the future.

Railway Ramps Up Preparations for the Big Day

The excitement is real! Railway officials are leaving no stone unturned. The Vande Metro rake is expected to arrive in Bihar shortly. Once it does, trial runs will begin without delay. This isn’t just another train—this is India’s ‘Namo Bharat’ Rapid Rail, known for its metro-like comfort and exceptional efficiency.

PM Modi to Inaugurate Key Rail Projects on April 24

Mark your calendar—Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be launching multiple railway projects from Jhanjharpur on April 24. Sources suggest this includes:

A new express train from Saharsa to Supaul The Amrit Bharat Express between Saharsa and Mumbai, flagged off virtually by the PM himself

A new express train from Saharsa to Supaul

The Amrit Bharat Express between Saharsa and Mumbai, flagged off virtually by the PM himself

What Makes the Vande Metro So Special? Also known as the Namo Bharat Rapid Rail, this train will be the first of its kind in Bihar, offering: A top speed of 130 km/h 12 to 16 fully air-conditioned coaches Seating for over 1,000 passengers Standing capacity for more than 2,000 travelers This means more people can travel comfortably and quickly, even during peak hours. Bihar Govt Sets Mission Mode to Open Degree Colleges in Every Block | 350 Colleges Approved for 2025

Big Leap for Bihar: College in Every Block Now a Reality

Bihar is rewriting its education map! The state government has officially launched the process to set up one affiliated degree college in every block. For generations, students in rural areas had to either migrate or abandon their dreams of higher education. That’s about to change.

This initiative is more than just policy—it’s a promise to bridge the rural-urban education gap across Bihar.

350 Colleges Approved in FY 2025–26

Under the 2025–26 budget, the Bihar government has allocated resources to establish 350 affiliated degree colleges. The Education Department, led by Secretary Ajay Yadav, is steering the process with urgency and clarity.

Instead of waiting for proposals, the department has already started marking land in each eligible block where no affiliated college exists.

Land Requirement: Clear and Actionable

To streamline the rollout, the department has set specific land criteria:

5 acres for rural blocks 2.5 acres for urban areas

5 acres for rural blocks

2.5 acres for urban areas

This clarity allows district authorities to begin their groundwork without delay. In fact, District Magistrates have already received a list of such blocks and the necessary instructions to begin immediate land verification.

Why It Matters: Education Meets Opportunity

This is not just about adding buildings—it’s about building futures. Here’s what this move brings:

Equal opportunity for students in all regions Reduced dropout rates, especially among rural girls Less migration, more retention of talent in local communities Boost to local economies through employment and infrastructure

Equal opportunity for students in all regions

Reduced dropout rates, especially among rural girls

Less migration, more retention of talent in local communities

Boost to local economies through employment and infrastructure

Ajay Yadav Leads from the Front

Ajay Yadav, Secretary of the Bihar Education Department, has signed and issued the official directive. Instead of keeping it on paper, he’s pushing for real-time execution, aligning district officials with the timeline. His leadership reflects a clear intent—every block deserves access to higher education.

What’s Next? A Phased Rollout

The colleges will not pop up overnight, but they will emerge in phases. The first step—identifying and reporting suitable land plots—is already underway. Once this step finishes, the government will proceed with the construction and affiliation process.

Communities, especially in backward regions, are now hopeful. Their children won’t just go to school—they’ll graduate from college without leaving their hometowns.

Bihar’s Bold Step: Mahila Samvad to Reach 48,000 Villages and Empower 2 Crore Women

“अब सुनवाई ही नहीं, समाधान भी होगा — गाँव की हर महिला की आवाज़ सरकार तक पहुंचेगी।”

From April 18, Bihar is set to witness one of its most ambitious people-led programs—Mahila Samvad. Over the next two months, this initiative will span 48,000 villages, involving nearly 2 crore women. It’s not a speech—it’s a two-way dialogue. And it’s all about real change.

What Is Mahila Samvad All About?

At its core, Mahila Samvad is a statewide initiative by the Nitish Kumar-led Bihar Government, aimed at creating direct communication with women at the grassroots. The Rural Development Department, in partnership with Jeevika, is conducting this campaign with a simple yet powerful goal—to listen, learn, and act.

To ensure inclusivity, the dialogues will happen in two daily shifts:

Morning: 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM Evening: 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM

Morning: 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM

Evening: 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM

Because women’s lives are busy and layered, the program respects their time and routine.

How the Government Plans to Engage

Every single day, 1,200 villages will host these sessions. That’s not all—600 Digital Awareness Vans (Jagrukta Raths) will travel across the state to reach even the most remote locations. These vans won’t just display government schemes. They’ll also serve as mobile feedback points.

Importantly, the government wants to know:

What challenges women face in daily life How they perceive development What support they actually need

What challenges women face in daily life

How they perceive development

What support they actually need

Rather than assuming, the government is asking.

Real Problems, Real Voices, Real Solutions

Unlike many top-down awareness campaigns, Mahila Samvad believes in bottom-up change. Problems shared during these dialogues won’t stop at discussion. In fact, they will be recorded and forwarded to the respective district headquarters.

Eventually, based on the insights gathered, custom solutions will be crafted for each locality. This ensures that feedback turns into actionable steps, not forgotten promises.

Why Muzaffarpur is a Key Focus

Interestingly, Muzaffarpur will host the highest number of Mahila Samvad events. The region, known for its active women-led groups under Jeevika, has become a model for participatory development.

This strategic focus ensures that feedback from high-participation districts can guide other areas more effectively.

More Than a Dialogue—It’s a Movement

While this initiative may align with the upcoming election season, it also reflects a larger shift in governance. It represents active listening and community-centered leadership. And more importantly, it signals a government that wants to reach its people on their terms.

When women from every background—farmers, homemakers, teachers, workers—get to voice their thoughts, the outcome is not just inclusive. It’s transformational.

Your Voice Matters Too

title: Bihar Becomes India’s No.1 State in Free Medicine Distribution
summary: Bihar Sets a New National Benchmark in Free Medicine Distribution Once known for its crumbling health infrastructure, Bihar has now emerged as India’s leader in free medicine supply—delivering over 611 essential medicines
content:
Bihar Sets a New National Benchmark in Free Medicine Distribution

Once known for its crumbling health infrastructure, Bihar has now emerged as India’s leader in free medicine supply—delivering over 611 essential medicines to patients across the state.

This remarkable transformation has brought affordable healthcare within reach of millions. And it’s not just a statistic; it’s a story of lives saved, families supported, and hope restored.

From 47 to 611: A Giant Leap in Medicine Availability

In 2006, government hospitals in Bihar offered just 47 types of medicines. Today, the list includes 611 medicines and 132 medical consumables and devices, covering treatments from viral infections to cancer care.

These medicines are available across government hospitals and health centres—absolutely free of cost.

This expansion means that patients no longer need to run to private pharmacies for critical medicines. Everything they need is often just a consultation away.

10X Rise in Medicine Supply and Budget

Over the last 20 years, the state’s budget for medicine supply has increased tenfold. From a modest beginning, the spending has now touched ₹762 crore in FY 2024–25.

As per official projections, it may reach ₹1100 crore by FY 2025–26. This investment has ensured uninterrupted supply, even of high-cost drugs.

No Patient Left Behind: Medicines for All

The goal is simple—every patient should receive the medicine they need.

From OPD to IPD, from urban hospitals to rural clinics, free medicine distribution ensures access to:

Life-saving emergency drugs Cancer, asthma, arthritis, and allergy medications Antibiotics and anti-viral treatments Blood-thinners and anti-allergic formulations

Life-saving emergency drugs

Cancer, asthma, arthritis, and allergy medications

Antibiotics and anti-viral treatments

Blood-thinners and anti-allergic formulations

This coverage means patients don’t delay treatment due to cost. That’s a massive win for public health.

Ranked No.1 in National Medicine Distribution

Bihar’s performance has been recognised nationally. According to the DVDMS (Drug and Vaccine Distribution Management System) portal, Bihar has consistently ranked #1 in medicine supply and distribution for the past five months.

This ranking reflects the state’s efficiency in managing procurement, inventory, and timely delivery to health centres.

A Gamechanger for Low-Income Families

Earlier, even a basic illness could push families into debt. Now, with free medicines readily available, patients no longer need to spend on costly prescriptions.

This shift has made healthcare more inclusive. It’s no longer about who can afford treatment, but about who needs it.

The Timeline of Progress

Here’s how the journey unfolded:

2006: Only 47 medicines available. 2008: Expanded to 33 medicines for OPD and 112 for IPD patients. 2023: 611 medicines and 132 consumables listed under free distribution.

2006: Only 47 medicines available.

2008: Expanded to 33 medicines for OPD and 112 for IPD patients.

2023: 611 medicines and 132 consumables listed under free distribution.

Each phase of progress brought essential care to more people—and built trust in the public health system.

A New Chapter in Bihar’s Healthcare Story

Bihar’s free medicine policy is more than a government initiative. It’s a public movement that’s improving health outcomes and saving lives.

It proves that focused reforms and consistent delivery can create change that touches every household.

content:
Bihar Goes Digital: Govt Begins Digitising Property Records Dating Back to 1908!

Bihar Launches Mega Digitisation Drive to Preserve Property Records Since 1908

Imagine being able to access your great-grandfather’s land deed with just a few clicks. That’s no longer a dream in Bihar. In a historic move that blends legacy with technology, the Bihar government has embarked on one of its most ambitious digitisation projects yet—scanning and securing over 5 crore registered documents dating back to 1908.

Preserving Bihar’s Century-Old Land History

Led by the Prohibition, Excise, and Registration Department, this digitisation effort focuses on preserving property documents that were once handwritten and stored in fragile paper format. The initiative aims to improve transparency, reduce legal disputes, and streamline land ownership verifications across the state.

As per officials, documents will be digitised year-wise—starting with the most recent (1995-1990), then moving backwards (1990-1947, followed by 1947-1908).

As per officials, documents will be digitised year-wise—starting with the most recent (1995-1990), then moving backwards (1990-1947, followed by 1947-1908).

Completed Work & What’s Next

The government has already digitised 2.34 crore registered deeds from 1995 to 2025. The fresh phase targets the remaining 5 crore deeds that pre-date this period. These documents mostly include property deeds, which play a vital role in both legal ownership and land transfer processes.

Tenders have been issued, and agencies are selected for this mammoth job. The goal? To complete the entire process in the next fiscal year.

Why This Matters to Every Landowner

With digitised records, landowners will easily access their title deeds, eliminating the long-standing hassle of physically visiting government offices or relying on intermediaries. More importantly, this move will help resolve land disputes—many of which have been stuck in legal limbo due to missing or unclear paperwork.

Boosting Revenue & Reforming the System

This drive isn’t just about digital convenience. It’s also showing results in numbers. The registration department exceeded its revenue targets in FY 2024-25, collecting ₹7,648 crore against a target of ₹7,500 crore. In contrast, the previous year brought in ₹6,170 crore.

Officials believe that improved processes, including paperless registrations in select offices and faster access to records, will further enhance service delivery and government earnings.

More Reforms on the Way

In addition to digitisation, the department is:

Launching paperless registration of documents in four pilot offices. Setting up three new registration offices at Birpur (Supaul), Sonbarsa (Saharsa), and Paliganj (Patna). Monitoring progress through special land surveys, which are expected to be complete by December 2026.

Launching paperless registration of documents in four pilot offices.

Setting up three new registration offices at Birpur (Supaul), Sonbarsa (Saharsa), and Paliganj (Patna).

Monitoring progress through special land surveys, which are expected to be complete by December 2026.

Ministerial Action and Accountability

Revenue Minister Sanjay Saraogi recently chaired a review meeting to assess the pace of digitisation and land survey work. He instructed officials to accelerate the survey process, particularly in 20 districts where the first phase has already begun. In East and West Champaran, where Phase II is underway, he expressed concern over delays in receiving self-declared forms and genealogical charts from landowners.

He also called on settlement officers and field staff to physically visit camps and help citizens submit required documentation for land title verification.

Digital Identity Revolution for Bihar Farmers Begins in Arwal—4,474 to Get Smart IDs!

Arwal Farmers Step Into the Digital Age—Smart IDs Now a Reality!In a bold leap toward agricultural empowerment, Arwal district in Bihar has launched a transformative initiative that will redefine the way farmers connect with government schemes. Through a unique pilot project, 4,474 farmers are now set to receive their very own 11-digit digital identification cards—a step that brings precision, accessibility, and dignity to the forefront of rural India.

Why This Matters: A Direct Gateway to Government Benefits

For far too long, many farmers in Bihar have struggled to access timely and direct support. This registry process—spearheaded by the Department of Agriculture—is here to change that. By creating individual digital identities, farmers will now receive benefits without the usual delays or middlemen interference.

To make this vision a reality, farmer registration camps have been set up across 10 selected revenue villages. The response? Overwhelming participation, real-time digital processing, and a renewed sense of hope in the farming community.

Tech at the Roots: Face Recognition & e-KYC in Action

Gone are the days of endless paperwork. Farmers now go through face recognition technology and e-KYC verification to confirm their identities. It’s fast, secure, and eliminates duplication or fraud.

What’s more, Agricultural Coordinators and Revenue Officers have joined hands for this mission. While coordinators handle the e-KYC, revenue officers take care of land verification—also known as “bucketing”—to make sure everything is accurate down to the last detail.

summary: Canteens, Identity Cards & Women Empowerment: Bihar’s Groundbreaking Move to Strengthen Blocks via JEEViKA Bihar Steps Boldly Forward—Canteens in Every Block, Led by Empowered Women Bihar isn’t just planning change—it’s making it
content:
Canteens, Identity Cards & Women Empowerment: Bihar’s Groundbreaking Move to Strengthen Blocks via JEEViKA

Bihar Steps Boldly Forward—Canteens in Every Block, Led by Empowered Women

Bihar isn’t just planning change—it’s making it happen. In a major development, the state government has announced that every block headquarters will soon host a special canteen. These canteens will cater not only to government employees but also to the general public, offering clean, affordable meals every day.

More importantly, the responsibility to run these canteens will lie with the women of JEEViKA Self-Help Groups (SHGs). That’s where the real impact lies.

Where Meals Meet Empowerment

Rural Development Minister Shrawan Kumar has taken a decisive step. He directed officials to implement this initiative through JEEViKA groups, ensuring it creates real opportunities for rural women. This isn’t just a welfare scheme—it’s a livelihood mission.

These canteens won’t only serve meals; they’ll serve confidence, skill-building, and dignity. By involving SHGs directly, the government is turning community kitchens into engines of change.

Identity Cards for JEEViKA Didis: A Long Overdue Recognition

To strengthen the identity and status of women involved in JEEViKA, the government will issue official ID cards. For the first time, these women will carry proof of their hard work and contribution.

Moreover, the administration plans to launch tailoring centers in community buildings across panchayats. These centers will train women in stitching and design, paving the way for self-employment.

Boosting Local Economy with Rural Haats

In addition to the canteens and sewing hubs, Bihar will set up rural haats—vibrant markets where SHGs can showcase and sell their products. These platforms will allow women to expand their reach, access more customers, and earn a fair income.

The plan also includes maize processing units, led by JEEViKA Didis. These units will create local jobs, reduce crop wastage, and add value to agriculture.

Lifting Traditional Artisans Through Focused Schemes

The government hasn’t ignored traditional artisans and micro-entrepreneurs. People engaged in trades like puffed rice selling, pottery, or utensil making will now benefit from targeted financial schemes.

By offering these workers skill training and credit support, Bihar aims to uplift small-scale livelihoods in a sustainable manner.

Urban SHGs Get Equal Importance

While rural areas remain the focus, urban SHGs are receiving attention too. Minister Shrawan Kumar clearly instructed officials to prioritize both rural and urban groups equally. He warned that failure to deliver results will attract disciplinary action.

This push ensures that the benefits of empowerment aren’t limited by geography.

Leaders Driving the Mission

content:
Akasa Air Soars into Bihar: Daily Darbhanga–Hyderabad Flights Redefine Regional Travel

Bihar’s Skies Just Got Busier – And Brighter

Akasa Air, one of India’s fastest-growing airlines, has made a confident entry into Bihar. It has launched daily flights connecting Darbhanga and Hyderabad, making travel simpler and faster for thousands. What’s more, a smart stopover in Delhi improves access from other parts of the country.

This move doesn’t just serve convenience—it opens new doors for mobility and development.

Why Darbhanga? Why Now?

Darbhanga, long celebrated for its culture, music, and Mithila heritage, deserves better connectivity. Until now, poor transport options have kept this gem underexplored.

With this new route, Akasa Air brings the city into the mainstream air travel map. As a result, tourists, business travellers, and students can now reach Darbhanga more easily than ever before.

In fact, with Darbhanga added, Akasa Air now connects 28 destinations across India. This expansion underlines the airline’s aggressive push to connect underserved regions.

A Real Boost for Bihar’s Economic Momentum

Air travel often signals growth, and this flight does just that. Instead of long train journeys, people can now fly quickly and affordably. Entrepreneurs will find better access to markets. Students can pursue education far from home without logistical stress. Families can reunite with fewer hurdles.

Moreover, Hyderabad being a major tech, business, and medical hub makes the connection even more valuable for Bihar residents.

This route doesn’t just carry passengers—it carries possibilities.

Akasa Air’s Strategic Play in Regional India

Akasa Air (@AkasaAir) is showing exactly how regional air travel should be done. Rather than chasing only big metros, it focuses on building meaningful regional links.

With efficient service and competitive pricing, the airline continues to grow its footprint rapidly. More importantly, it keeps people at the center of its strategy.

Choosing Darbhanga is not just good business—it’s a smart move toward inclusive connectivity.

What This Means for You

Breaking the Silence: How Surbhi Kumari is Revolutionizing Menstrual Health in Bihar

A City of Traditions and Taboos

Gaya, Bihar—revered as the Moksha City—is known for its deep-rooted traditions. However, in a place where taboos often go unchallenged, a young girl once faced an unspoken embarrassment—the arrival of her first period.

But this is not just her story.

The Harsh Reality of Menstrual Taboos

Like countless others, Surbhi Kumari grew up in an environment where menstruation was wrapped in silence and misinformation. Yet, unlike many, she refused to accept it as normal.

She saw women in rural Bihar using unhygienic materials like sand, ash, and dirty cloth. Consequently, this wasn’t just a personal challenge—it was a crisis.

The Turning Point

In 2011, while working with JPAL, Surbhi witnessed firsthand the dire state of menstrual health in low-income communities. As a result, this experience became the catalyst for her mission to drive real change.

The Birth of SumArth

In 2019, Surbhi co-founded SumArth, a social enterprise dedicated to dismantling menstrual taboos and providing sustainable hygiene solutions. Since then, her initiative has:

Empowered over 20,000 women and 5,000 adolescent girls with menstrual education. Introduced affordable sanitary products and menstrual cups to marginalized communities. Established a fully automatic sanitary pad-making unit, run by rural women, ensuring economic independence.

As a result, women who once hid their struggles now advocate for change, embracing hygiene with dignity.

A Movement for Change

Surbhi Kumari’s journey is an inspiring testament to awareness, resilience, and action. Over time, she has transformed personal pain into a powerful movement, rewriting the narrative of menstrual health in Bihar—one woman at a time.

# Meet the Bihar Scientist Who Discovered Plastic-Eating Bacteria & Got Invited to an International Conference!

A Breakthrough Against Plastic Pollution

Plastic pollution is a global crisis. However, a groundbreaking discovery by Dr. Raj Sardar from Bihar is offering a ray of hope. A biotechnology expert at Central University of South Bihar, Dr. Sardar has identified Micrococcus flex, a bacteria that can biodegrade plastic and convert it into biomass. This revolutionary research could redefine waste management and environmental conservation.

Recognition on the Global Stage

Dr. Raj Sardar’s pioneering work has earned him an invitation to present his findings at the American Society for Microbiology’s Scientific Conference in Los Angeles this June. Notably, being a member of the world’s oldest and largest microbiology society, this is a prestigious recognition of his contributions to environmental science.

The Science Behind Plastic Degradation

Unlike conventional plastic disposal methods that release toxic gases such as dioxins and carbon monoxide, Dr. Sardar’s research offers a sustainable solution. His study, conducted at CSIR’s laboratory, confirms that Micrococcus flex forms a biofilm on plastic surfaces, slowly breaking them down. Furthermore, within just 30 days, this bacteria reduces plastic weight by approximately 2%—a breakthrough in microbial plastic degradation.

Why This Discovery Matters

Reduces Greenhouse Gas Emissions: Traditional plastic burning increases greenhouse gas emissions by 4%. Consequently, this innovation could help mitigate climate change. Eco-Friendly Waste Management: Replacing harmful disposal methods with biological solutions ensures a healthier environment. Potential for Large-Scale Implementation: Future applications may include integrating this bacteria into industrial waste treatment, making waste management more efficient.

Published in a High-Impact Journal

Dr. Sardar’s research has already gained international attention. In fact, it has been published in the World Journal of Microbiology and Biotechnology, a reputed journal in the field. This further validates the potential of his work in shaping the future of plastic waste management.

Dreams Crushed Over One Mark, Bihar Girl’s Plea Gets National Attention

In a heart-wrenching turn of events, Khushbu Kumari from Danapur, Bihar, saw her dream of becoming a doctor slip away due to societal norms and financial constraints. But what happened next turned her story into a national conversation.

“One Mark Took Away My Dream”: The Pain of Gender Bias

Khushbu, an aspiring science student, was forced into the arts stream after failing to meet a strict condition set by her parents. “If you score over 400 marks, you can take science,” they said. She scored 399. Just one mark short.

“In my house, boys have complete freedom to study, but girls don’t. We don’t even get a phone for studying,” she shared in a viral video, breaking down in tears.

Her father, Upendra Rai, defended the decision, citing financial limitations. “Science education is expensive. We couldn’t afford it,” he admitted.

Viral Video Sparks Action: Help Arrives

As the video gained traction, a powerful response followed. The Union government stepped in, assuring Khushbu of full support for her enrollment in a good college.

During a video call arranged by Patna District Magistrate Chandrashekhar Singh, she was encouraged to stay focused. “Do not worry, my child. Help is on the way. Study well and don’t hold anything against your parents.”

The administration has now stepped in to secure Khushbu’s admission into Class 11 with a Biology major for the 2025-27 session.

Education Over Barriers: A Step Towards Change

Khushbu’s story is a stark reminder of the gender bias and financial struggles many girls in India still face. However, her resilience and the power of social media have ignited a movement.

title: From Jail to Teacher: Bihar’s Vipin Kumar Gets Government Job While in Handcuffs
summary: From Prison to Classroom: The Unbelievable Journey of a Bihar Man Who Became a Government Teacher A Scene That Shocked Everyone The image of a man in handcuffs walking onto a stage
content:
A Scene That Shocked Everyone

The image of a man in handcuffs walking onto a stage to receive his government teaching appointment letter left the audience in awe. The story of Vipin Kumar, a prisoner from Bihar’s Beur Jail, is unlike anything seen before. Despite being behind bars for 18 months under the POCSO Act, he successfully cleared the TRE-3 examination and secured a government teaching job.

Vipin Kumar’s Struggles and Triumph

Vipin, a native of Airki village, Mohanpur block, Gaya, was once a respected teacher at a private coaching institute in Patna’s Saguna Mor. In 2023, he was accused under the POCSO Act and arrested. However, he has always claimed innocence, stating that rival coaching institutes framed him in a conspiracy.

While waiting for justice, Vipin did not let his circumstances define him. Even in jail, he continued his studies, determined to build a future. His hard work paid off when he cleared Bihar’s Teacher Recruitment Exam (TRE-3) and became eligible for a government teaching position.

The Moment That Stunned Bihar

On March 9, 2025, during a grand ceremony at the Mahabodhi Cultural Center in Bodh Gaya, Bihar Government Minister Nitish Mishra personally handed over the appointment letter to Vipin Kumar. However, the sight of a prisoner receiving his appointment letter while in handcuffs left many speechless. For the first time in Bihar’s history, a jailed man officially became a government teacher.

With heavy security, Vipin was escorted from Beur Jail to Bodh Gaya for the event. As his name was announced, he walked onto the stage, still bound by chains. The hall filled with murmurs as people struggled to process the surreal moment. Was this a sign of justice, perseverance, or irony?

“I Want to Serve Society” – Vipin Kumar’s Emotional Words

After receiving his appointment, Vipin spoke to the media. “I have always wanted to educate children and serve society. Even inside jail, I never gave up on my dreams. Once I am free, I will dedicate my life to teaching and shaping young minds,” he said.

His words resonated with many. Should a person who has not been convicted yet be denied a chance at a better life? Minister Nitish Mishra emphasized that the Bihar government is committed to providing deserving candidates their due opportunities. He added that Vipin’s journey could inspire many others facing adversity.

What’s Next for Vipin Kumar?

Despite securing the job, Vipin remains in judicial custody as his trial is still ongoing. His fate depends on the court’s verdict. If proven innocent, he will begin his teaching career. If found guilty, his appointment could be canceled.

The incident has sparked debates across Bihar. Can justice and opportunity coexist? Should someone accused, but not yet convicted, be given such an opportunity? Vipin’s story challenges traditional perspectives, making people rethink rehabilitation and second chances.

title: 92 Thai Buddhist Pilgrims Walk to Lauria, Honoring Ancient Sites in Bihar
summary: A Sacred Journey: 92 Thai Buddhist Pilgrims Walk to Lauria, Honoring Ancient Sites A Spiritual Walk Across Borders In an awe-inspiring display of devotion, 92 Buddhist pilgrims from Thailand arrived in Lauria,
content:
A Spiritual Walk Across Borders

In an awe-inspiring display of devotion, 92 Buddhist pilgrims from Thailand arrived in Lauria, Bihar, as part of their sacred journey. Walking thousands of kilometers, their pilgrimage spans historical Buddhist sites across India and Nepal, retracing the footsteps of Lord Buddha.

From Thailand to Bihar: The Path of Enlightenment

The journey began on February 19, 2024, in Thailand. Since then, the pilgrims have visited Bodh Gaya, Rajgir, Vaishali, Kesaria, and Kushinagar, before reaching Lauria. Their next destinations include Rampurva in Gaunaha and finally Lumbini, Nepal, where they will complete their pilgrimage on April 1, 2024.

Paying Homage at Lauria’s Buddhist Heritage

Upon arrival in Lauria, the group rested overnight at Vishunpurwa Pokhara Ground in Siswania Panchayat. The following morning, they visited Nandangarh, a site believed to house the remains of Buddha’s relics. After offering prayers, they walked to the famous Ashokan Pillar, built by Emperor Ashoka, an iconic symbol of Buddhism’s spread.

The Deeper Significance of This Pilgrimage

For these pilgrims, this journey is not just a physical one but a spiritual experience. Walking through the same lands where Buddha once preached, they seek enlightenment, peace, and blessings. The sight of monks clad in saffron robes, chanting mantras, and walking barefoot has mesmerized locals, fostering a sense of cultural unity.

Bihar: A Global Buddhist Destination

With sites like Bodh Gaya, Vaishali, Kesaria, and Lauria, Bihar holds immense significance in Buddhist history. This pilgrimage highlights its global appeal, attracting devotees from around the world.

title: Bihar’s Bold Step: Empowering Women Against Domestic Violence
summary: Bihar Takes Action: 140 Protection Officers Appointed to Tackle Domestic Violence Domestic violence continues to affect countless women in Bihar. However, the government is now stepping up to address this crisis. In
content:
Domestic violence continues to affect countless women in Bihar. However, the government is now stepping up to address this crisis. In a significant move, 140 ‘protection officers’ have been appointed to assist survivors with legal, medical, and emotional support. This initiative is expected to create a safer environment for women and provide them with the resources needed to break free from abusive situations.

The Stark Reality of Domestic Violence in Bihar

The statistics are alarming. In 2024, the National Commission for Women (NCW) received 25,743 complaints of domestic violence across India. Bihar accounted for 4.8% of these cases, revealing the urgent need for intervention.

Although legal protections exist under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) of 2005, many victims still hesitate to seek help. Social stigma, fear of retaliation, and lack of awareness often prevent women from reporting abuse. This is why the presence of protection officers is so crucial in bridging the gap between survivors and the support systems available to them.

How Will Protection Officers Help?

These officers will play a critical role in supporting victims and ensuring justice. Their responsibilities include:

✔️ Assisting survivors in filing legal complaints✔️ Providing access to medical and psychological care✔️ Connecting victims with shelter homes and legal aid✔️ Raising awareness about women’s rights and available resources

By acting as a direct link between survivors and the justice system, they aim to empower women and encourage them to seek help without fear.

Challenges That Still Need to Be Addressed

While this initiative marks a significant step forward, several challenges remain. Many women hesitate to report abuse due to deep-rooted cultural norms. Additionally, limited resources and bureaucratic delays often slow down the justice process, leaving survivors in prolonged distress.

Addressing domestic violence requires more than just legal intervention. Communities must actively participate in creating a culture that condemns abuse. Education, awareness campaigns, and stronger law enforcement will be key factors in driving lasting change.

Change is happening, but more voices need to rise against domestic violence. If you or someone you know is facing abuse, don’t stay silent. Reach out for help, support organizations working for women’s rights, and speak up against injustice.

When the roads were choked with endless traffic, seven fearless young men from Bihar found an extraordinary way to reach Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh Mela—by sailing 275 km on the Ganga! Their journey wasn’t just about avoiding gridlocks; it was a thrilling adventure fueled by innovation, perseverance, and an unbreakable bond with the sacred river.

Beating Traffic With a Bold Idea

With the Maha Kumbh attracting millions, the highways to Prayagraj turned into parking lots. But Manu Chaudhary, an experienced boatman from Kamhariya village, had a game-changing idea—why not take the river instead?

Along with his friends Sumant, Sandeep, Sukhdev, Aadu, Ravindra, and Ramesh, he prepped a motorized boat, stocked it with essentials, and set sail from Buxar, Bihar. What started as a practical solution soon became an unforgettable voyage of faith and resilience.

Navigating the Ganga: A Modern-Day Pilgrimage

The 275-km water journey wasn’t just about rowing—it required smart navigation. Using Google Maps, they charted their path, just like highway commuters. Even in pitch darkness, technology guided them through the river’s winding course.

They planned meticulously, carrying a gas cylinder, stove, food supplies, and even an extra engine as a backup. Every detail mattered because the round-trip covered approximately 550 km and took 84 hours!

A Journey of Faith & Grit

For these young men, the trip wasn’t just about reaching Maha Kumbh—it was a tribute to the Ganga’s eternal spirit. Their journey showcased the perfect blend of tradition and technology, courage and calculation.

As their boat touched the ghats of Prayagraj, they didn’t just arrive at the Maha Kumbh; they made history on the Ganga’s mighty waves.

From Tragedy to Determination

Navneet’s life took a devastating turn when he lost his father in a road accident in Class 7. With his mother struggling to make ends meet, he faced the harsh realities of life early on. Despite these challenges, he remained dedicated to his education, refusing to let adversity define his future.

Navneet initially aspired to join the National Defense Academy (NDA), but his -2 myopia crushed that dream. Rather than giving up, he shifted his focus to other government exams. He pursued a degree in Economics from Ambedkar University, Delhi, while preparing for competitive exams alongside.

Combined Defense Services (CDS) UPSC CAPF (Secured Rank 37) UGC NET JRF

On his third attempt, Navneet finally cracked the UPSC Civil Services Exam, securing an All India Rank of 499. In his words, “Seeing this change has brought so much happiness to me.” His mother summed it up perfectly: “I lived 15 years in a single day.”

title: Cybercrime in Bihar: Are You the Next Target? Stay Alert & Stay Safe!
summary: Cybercrime in Bihar: Are You the Next Target? Stay Alert & Stay Safe! The digital world is a double-edged sword. While technology brings convenience, it also opens doors to cyber threats. Every
content:
The digital world is a double-edged sword. While technology brings convenience, it also opens doors to cyber threats. Every day, countless people in Bihar fall prey to cybercrime. So, are you prepared to protect yourself?

The Rising Threat of Cybercrime in Bihar

Cyber fraud, phishing scams, and identity theft are increasing at an alarming rate. In fact, criminals are finding new ways to deceive innocent users. From fake job offers to UPI fraud, no one is safe unless they stay informed. Therefore, awareness is the first step toward protection.

Common Cyber Crimes You Need to Know

1. Online Banking Frauds

Cybercriminals use fake calls and phishing links to steal banking details. Consequently, never share OTPs or passwords.

2. Social Media Scams

Hackers access accounts and demand ransom. Thus, always enable two-factor authentication.

3. Fake Shopping Websites

Fraudsters create fake e-commerce sites to trap buyers. Hence, always check for HTTPS and reviews before purchasing.

4. Job Scams

Many job seekers fall for fake employment opportunities. As a result, verify companies before making any payments.

5. Lottery and Gift Frauds

If you get a message about winning a lottery you never entered, it’s a scam. So, ignore and report it immediately.

How to Protect Yourself?

Use Strong Passwords – A mix of letters, numbers, and symbols makes accounts safer. Verify Sources – Don’t click on unknown links or download files from untrusted sources. Update Software – Regular updates fix security vulnerabilities. Thus, keeping your system updated is crucial. Educate Your Family – Teach them about cyber threats to prevent future scams. After all, awareness can save them from fraud.

Where to Report Cyber Crimes?

If you become a victim, act fast. You can report cyber fraud at:

Bihar Cyber Crime Portal: https://biharpolice.bih.nic.in National Cyber Crime Portal: https://cybercrime.gov.in Cyber Helpline: Dial 1930 for immediate help

They received the prestigious President’s Medal for Distinguished Services (PSM) just before Republic Day. This award recognizes individuals for their exceptional service over a long period.

Seven other officials, including police officers and members of fire services, Home Guard & Civil Defence (HG&CD), and correctional services, also received the President’s Medal for Meritorious Service (MSM). The President’s Medal for Distinguished Service (PSM)

The PSM is the highest award for police officers. It honors individuals who have completed 25 years or more of service in the police or security organizations. This year, Kassey Suhita Anupam and Anil Kumar received the PSM for their outstanding leadership and contributions.

title: From Football Fields to Visionaries: How Bihar’s Rural Girls Are Becoming Footballers and Optometrists
summary: In the heart of Bihar, just 50 kilometers from Patna, lies a remarkable story of transformation—a journey from football fields to thriving careers. The Akhand Jyoti Eye Hospital is not just a
content:
In the heart of Bihar, just 50 kilometers from Patna, lies a remarkable story of transformation—a journey from football fields to thriving careers. The Akhand Jyoti Eye Hospital is not just a hub for eye care; it’s a powerhouse for empowering underprivileged girls. Through an extraordinary program called “Football to Eyeball,” this institution is reshaping futures, blending education, football, and professional training to turn dreams into reality.

A Unique Blend of Sports and Education

Since 2009, 725 rural girls have become self-reliant through this initiative. These girls are not only excelling as optometrists and technicians but also proving their mettle on the football field. Out of them, 15 have already represented Bihar at the national level, with Sonia Rai even captaining the state women’s football team.

What makes this initiative unique is its dual approach:

Free residential education and training for girls who have completed their 10th or 12th grades. Mandatory football sessions to instill discipline, teamwork, and confidence.

The Vision Behind the Program

Mritunjay Tiwari, CEO of the Akhand Jyoti Eye Hospital and a former professional footballer from Kolkata, started this initiative. Inspired by a simple yet poignant scene of rural girls kicking a paper ball, he envisioned using football as a tool for empowerment.

The program isn’t limited to academics and sports. The girls complete foundational courses and graduate as optometrists, equipped with skills for sustainable employment. Astonishingly, 286 girls are currently enrolled, living, learning, and playing—completely free of cost.

Global Impact and Partnerships

The impact of “Football to Eyeball” reaches far beyond India. The program has ties with the Chelsea Football Club in London, which granted Tiwari an active membership. Inspired by this, Belgium initiated the Belgium Babes Football League, contributing to the cause with donations for every goal scored. This international collaboration highlights the program’s global resonance.

Breaking Stereotypes and Shattering Barriers

This initiative comes with one critical condition: parents must pledge not to marry off their daughters before the age of 23. This bold step ensures that the girls focus on their education and career without societal pressures holding them back.

The Numbers Speak Volumes

36% growth in self-reliance among rural girls in the region. Participation in 15 national-level football tournaments by program beneficiaries. Over 725 girls trained to date, with many pursuing higher education, including MBA and Ph.D. programs.

This transformative initiative demonstrates the power of combining sports, education, and unwavering determination. With every kick on the football field and every eye examination conducted, these girls are rewriting their destinies.

title: Incredible Village: Jagdishpur in Ujiarpur, Samastipur – 40 Years of Dispute-Free Harmony Without Police or Court Involvement
summary: A Beacon of Harmony: Jagdishpur Village, Samastipur – 40 Years of Peaceful Coexistence In a world filled with conflicts, Jagdishpur village in Samastipur stands as a shining example of harmony and unity.
content:
A Beacon of Harmony: Jagdishpur Village, Samastipur – 40 Years of Peaceful Coexistence

In a world filled with conflicts, Jagdishpur village in Samastipur stands as a shining example of harmony and unity. Located just 3 km from Ujiarpur, this small community of 80 families has achieved a rare feat—no legal disputes for over 40 years. Even minor disagreements never reach the police station or the village court; instead, they are resolved through dialogue and consensus.

The Unique Fabric of Jagdishpur

Education and awareness form the backbone of this Mahadalit-dominated village. With a population of about 700, the community collectively decides on matters, including whom to vote for in elections. The villagers reject harmful practices like child marriage, dowry, and substance abuse. They not only discourage these issues but actively work together to eliminate them.

Ward member Yogendra Paswan emphasizes education’s transformative role. Children attend the local primary school and Anganwadi center regularly. Older students study at nearby high schools. This commitment has led five villagers to become government school teachers.

Progress Amid Challenges

In 1985, the central government selected Jagdishpur for a development initiative. While progress has been slow, the village now enjoys roads, solar lights, and a water supply. The community’s resilience has earned recognition from local authorities.

Samastipur District Magistrate Roshan Kushwaha calls Jagdishpur “a pride not just for the district but for the nation.” Officials plan to enhance its infrastructure further.

Why Jagdishpur Stands Out

Jagdishpur’s ability to resolve disputes peacefully makes it extraordinary. While caste, religion, and property disputes divide other places, this village unites through dialogue. DSP Vivek Kumar Sharma describes it as “a perfect example of an ideal community.”

title: BPSC Re-Examination Today Amid Protests: All Eyes on Patna as Security Tightens
summary: When exams determine futures, fairness is non-negotiable. Today, the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) is conducting a re-examination for 12,000 candidates in Patna, following serious allegations of irregularities during the December 13
content:
When exams determine futures, fairness is non-negotiable. Today, the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC) is conducting a re-examination for 12,000 candidates in Patna, following serious allegations of irregularities during the December 13 exam. This crucial step aims to restore trust amidst mounting protests and heightened security.

Why the Re-Examination?

The re-exam specifically addresses concerns about the December test conducted at Bapu Pariksha Parisar, where procedural lapses were reported. Authorities have now split the candidates across 22 centres in Patna to ensure better management and transparency.

Unprecedented Security Measures

In a bid to prevent disruptions, Patna District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar has invoked Section 163 of the Criminal Procedure Code. This bans public gatherings of more than five people within a 100-metre radius of the exam centres. Demonstrations, processions, and even the use of loudspeakers are prohibited.

The restrictions will remain in effect from 8 AM to 5 PM today, particularly impacting prominent centres like P.N. Anglo Sanskrit High School and Government Girls High Secondary School in Shastri Nagar. Candidates are barred from carrying mobile phones or smart devices, ensuring that the examination environment remains secure.

The Protests Continue

Despite these efforts, discontent brews. On Friday, thousands of students took to the streets, disrupting rail and road traffic. Left-aligned student organisations even attempted to march to the Chief Minister’s residence. The protests escalated further as police resorted to force, leaving several demonstrators injured.

Adding fuel to the fire, Jan Suraj Party leader Prashant Kishor has begun an indefinite hunger strike at Gandhi Maidan. He demands accountability from the police and calls for the cancellation of the exam altogether.

A Critical Test for Authorities and Aspirants

As candidates prepare to rewrite their future, the authorities face the challenge of conducting a smooth and fair examination. The stakes are high for everyone involved.

title: Siwan Emerges as Bihar’s Leader in Overseas Aspirations, with Gopalganj and Patna Following Close Behind
summary: Dreaming big and reaching new heights, Bihar shines in the latest Passport Service report of 2024. Leading the charge is Siwan, setting an example of ambition and determination as the district tops
content:
Dreaming big and reaching new heights, Bihar shines in the latest Passport Service report of 2024. Leading the charge is Siwan, setting an example of ambition and determination as the district tops the state in passport applications and issuances.

Bihar’s Passport Revolution in Numbers

The Ministry of External Affairs reveals a remarkable milestone: Bihar issued 402,045 passports in 2024, a 4.5% increase from the previous year. Among the 422,914 applications received, 30% came from just three districts—Siwan, Gopalganj, and Patna.

1️⃣ Siwan: The frontrunner in sending people abroad. 2️⃣ Gopalganj: A close second with a surge in demand. 3️⃣ Patna: Securing the third spot as the state capital.

Addressing Challenges in Passport Services

However, challenges persist. Reports indicate a rise in passport applications based on forged documents, particularly from Siwan and Gopalganj. To combat this, mobile van camps, supported by the Labour Resources Department, are being organized to educate applicants and prevent fraud.

In the last year, over 500 complaints were filed across Bihar, highlighting instances of deceit in passport issuance and overseas job placements.

Innovations in Passport Services

Bihar’s passport ecosystem is evolving rapidly:

Police verification is now streamlined through the mPassport app, aiming to issue passports within a week. Post Office Passport Seva Kendras (POPSK) have expanded to 35 centers across 40 Lok Sabha constituencies.

New centers for 2025 are planned in Rajnagar (Jhanjharpur), Bhakhra (Vaishali), and Ram Nagar (Valmikinagar), ensuring greater accessibility.

Faster Clearance for Police Certificates

Police Clearance Certificates (PCCs) are integral to passport processing. On average, Bihar takes 12 days for PCC issuance. However, districts like Khagaria (5 days) and Nalanda (6 days) have set benchmarks for efficiency.

Empowering Applicants Through Feedback

Each month, the Regional Passport Office addresses the concerns of over 5,000 applicants via in-person meetings, social media platforms, email, and postal correspondence.
